editorial.dek: PerryCock climbs out of a 68.65-point hole on PhilthyPhil, Murrdawgs drop a season-high 220.85 on the team they sold Derrick Henry to, and four teams are now tied at 7-3. The commissioner started a running back on injured reserve. Again.

stories.h: PerryCock comes back from 68.65 down, and PhilthyPhil's bench curse switches positions
stories.body: PhilthyPhil's entire lineup played in the early Sunday window, and when it was over Phil led 151.55 to 82.9 with nothing left to do but watch. Then Christian McCaffrey dropped 48.3 in San Francisco's 46-40 win in Dallas, Ja'Marr Chase added 34.1 on Sunday night, and PerryCock won 165.3 to 151.55. Phil left 37.7 points on the bench, most in the league: Deebo Samuel Sr. (25.9) and Ryan Flournoy (19.1) sat behind Christian Watson (6.7) and Denzel Boston (2.6). Sleeper liked the starters, so it's the quarterback saga all over again in a new position group: defensible, wrong, and the best lineup wins by 23.95. PerryCock has won three straight and its playoff odds jumped from 82% to 91%. Phil is still 7-3, but the bye odds slipped from 69% to 64%.

stories.h: Four teams at 7-3, two byes, four weeks to sort it out
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor, PhilthyPhil, Bad Bunny's Bush and Bijan al Gaib are all 7-3, and only two of them get a week off in the playoffs. Murrdawgs sit on top thanks to points, with bye odds up from 43% to 56%. Phil is at 64%. Bijan al Gaib has won four straight and went from 16% to 36%. And Bad Bunny's Bush, which won six in a row from Week 3 to Week 8, has now lost two straight and watched its bye odds crash from 68% to 38%, the biggest drop of the week. jambosti went from first to third in one Sunday. Every game from here to Week 14 is a bye elimination game for somebody.

stories.h: Murrdawgs score 220.85 and turn the $400 race into a parade
stories.body: A week ago the points race had a 56.1-point gap at the top. Then Murrdawgs hung 220.85, the highest score of the 2026 season, while Bad Bunny's Bush put up 93.6. Murrdawgs now have 1,623.95. PerryCock is second, 132.0 back. PhilthyPhil is 177.1 back and Bad Bunny's Bush fell to 183.35 back. Four regular-season weeks are left, so the math says Connorj22 can start picking out what to buy with the $400. The rulebook says one more thing, though: a points leader who doesn't reach the championship game picks 1.10. The money's nice. December still counts.

stories.h: The 5-5 club has four members and the worst one holds the last playoff seat
stories.body: PerryCock, Geno-Cide Smith, CeeDeez Nutz and Cheesehead10 are all 5-5. PerryCock is fifth with a 76-34 all-play record and a 91% playoff shot after allowing a league-high 1,393.1 points. The sixth and final spot belongs to Geno-Cide Smith, whose playoff odds are 21%, the lowest of the three bubble teams at 5-5. CeeDeez Nutz fell from fifth to seventh and dropped from 59% to 35%. Cheesehead10 is eighth at 26%, and degr is lurking at 4-6 after jumping from 16% to 26% with two straight wins. Translation: the sim thinks the last ticket goes to whoever stops tripping first.

stories.h: The trade box score: Henry gets revenge on nobody, St. Brown gets it on his old team
stories.body: Murrdawgs traded Derrick Henry to ChrisUMD23 for a 2029 first last Thursday, the schedule made them play this week, and Henry scored 19.0 on Monday night in a 97.9-point loss. Amon-Ra St. Brown, who went from Open for Business (then closed for business) to Bijan al Gaib in Week 5, scored 25.8 against his old team in the biggest blowout of the season. A.J. Brown, sent from Bad Bunny's Bush to degr in Week 6, scored 4.7 in degr's win over Bad Bunny's and has since been ruled out with a hamstring injury. And Ollie Gordon II scored 15.5 for Cheesehead10 on Sunday, then got shipped to PhilthyPhil that same afternoon for a 2027 third and a 2028 second. Cheesehead10 is 5-5 and selling. Phil is 7-3 and buying. Everybody knows exactly who they are.

stories.h: Race for 1.02: NotGomes pulls away, and Cheesehead10 is the one smiling
stories.body: Matty Ice is the 1.01 in every simulation with an 846.75 Maximum Points For, 376.9 below anyone else. Non-playoff teams draft by reverse Max PF, so the real fight is for 1.02, and it just got less close. Open for Business sits at 1,223.65 and ChrisUMD23 at 1,263.15, a gap of 39.5 that was 12.79 a week ago. ChrisUMD23's best lineup was 130.15 in a blowout loss, Open for Business's was 103.45. Open for Business's first belongs to Cheesehead10 and projects at an average slot of 2.26. ChrisUMD23's belongs to Murrdawgs and projects at 3.33. Meanwhile NotGomes owns the 2027 firsts from degr and Bijan al Gaib, and both of those teams won this week. Rough Sunday to be a draft pick on that roster.

stories.h: CeeDeez Nutz come back on Murrdawgs and blow up the bye race
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor took a 16.75-point lead out of Thursday night and never saw it again. CeeDee Lamb dropped 35.5, Drake Maye added 27.25, DeMario Douglas turned an 8.8 projection into 17.2, and CeeDeez Nutz won 124.05 to 113.0.

stories.h: PhilthyPhil has now lost the quarterback coin flip three weeks running
stories.body: Week 6: Caleb Williams starts, C.J. Stroud scores 34.1 on the bench.

stories.h: PerryCock scores 190.15 and crashes the $400 points race
stories.body: A week ago this was a two-team race. Then PerryCock put up 190.15, the fourth-highest score of the season, and cut its deficit from 153.6 to 76.45.

news.h: PhilthyPhil trade two picks to Cheesehead10 for Ollie Gordon II
news.body: PhilthyPhil gets Ollie Gordon II (RB). Cheesehead10 gets 2027 Rd 3 (PhilthyPhil) and 2028 Rd 2 (PhilthyPhil). PhilthyPhil is 7-3 and second, and Cheesehead10 is 5-5 and eighth. After the trade PhilthyPhil owns one first-round pick and Cheesehead10 owns seven.

tradeAnalysis.headline: PhilthyPhil wins the Ollie Gordon II trade with Cheesehead10

takes.8: PhilthyPhil were 7-2 and second when they bought Ollie Gordon II, a 22-year-old running back scoring 13.68 points per game, for a 2027 third and a 2028 second. They came out 289 ahead in value, 17% of the deal. The two picks add up to 896, but the package adjustment counts the smaller pieces for less, so they come to 700 against Gordon's 989. PhilthyPhil are now 7-3 with the second-most points in the league, 1,446.85, and own one first-round pick, in 2029.
takes.3: Cheesehead10 was 4-5 and eighth, level on record with sixth place, when it sold Gordon's 13.68 points per game for two late picks and gave up 289 in value. The draft side covers most of that. Non-playoff teams draft in reverse order of Maximum Points For, and without Gordon its own 2027 first projects to an average slot of 5.05 instead of 5.49, a gain of 174 in the value of its 2027 picks. Cheesehead10 is now 5-5 and eighth with about a 31% playoff chance, and owns seven first-round picks and the league's second most valuable roster.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor win the Derrick Henry trade with ChrisUMD23

takes.2: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor were 6-2 and second when they sold Derrick Henry, 32 years old and scoring 16.25 points per game, for ChrisUMD23's 2029 first. They came out 355 ahead in value, 13% of the deal. It costs a contender real production: Murrdawgs are now 6-3 and lead the league with 1,403.1 points, 56.1 ahead of Bad Bunny's Bush in the race for the $400 points prize. They also own ChrisUMD23's 2027 first, so Henry's points raising ChrisUMD23's Max PF lower the value of Murrdawgs' 2027 picks by 29 in the draft projection.
takes.11: ChrisUMD23 was 3-5 and one game out of sixth when it paid a 2029 first for Derrick Henry, coming up 355 short in value. Henry adds 16.25 points per game to a team with 850.25 points, second fewest in the league, and ChrisUMD23 is now 3-6, one game behind 4-5 PerryCock for the last playoff spot. Losing does not help it in the draft, because Murrdawgs Massage Parlor own its 2027 first, which projects to an average slot of 3.25. ChrisUMD23 has the league's lowest roster value and one first-round pick left.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor and Cheesehead10 make an even trade for Tyler Allgeier

takes.2: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor, now 6-2 and second, paid a 2027 second valued at 660 for Tyler Allgeier, valued at 654, so the deal is even. Allgeier adds a 26-year-old running back with 86.1 points in eight games, 10.76 per game. Murrdawgs lead the league with 1,290.1 points, 52.7 ahead of Bad Bunny's Bush in the race for the $400 points prize. They still own four first-round picks but no longer have a 2027 second.
takes.3: Cheesehead10, now 4-4 and sixth, the last playoff spot, sold 10.76 points per game for a pick and came out 6 ahead in value. It already holds seven first-round picks and 22 picks in all, so this adds to a pile more than it fills a need. Selling Allgeier barely moves its own 2027 first, which projects to an average slot of 5.90 with the trade and 5.91 without it.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Open for Business wins the Tetairoa McMillan trade with Matty Ice

takes.1: Matty Ice went into Week 8 at 1-6 and in last place, and finished it 1-7. It paid two 2027 firsts, its own 2027 second and its own 2028 third for Tetairoa McMillan and Jaxson Dart, both 23, and loses the deal 3,882 to 5,036 in value (4,462 to 6,681 before the package adjustment). The two add 34.8 points per game on paper, with Dart's 17.95 coming from two games, and Matty Ice's own 2027 first still projects at 1.01 with or without them because its Max PF of 683.0 is the lowest in the league. It still owns seven first-round picks, three of them in 2027.
takes.10: Open for Business went into Week 8 at 4-3 and sixth, then lost to fall to 4-4 and seventh. It gave up 34.8 points per game for four picks and comes out 1,154 ahead in value, 12.9% of the deal. degr's first projects to an average slot of 5.8, Bijan al Gaib's to 9.37, and Matty Ice's second is an early one because Matty Ice projects at 1.01. It now owns three first-round picks, up from one, but not its own 2027 first: Cheesehead10 holds that one, and it projects at 2.03.

tradeAnalysis.headline: PerryCock wins the Michael Wilson trade with Open for Business

takes.6: PerryCock went into Week 8 at 2-5 and tenth, two games behind sixth, then won to reach 3-5 and eighth. It paid three late seconds for Michael Wilson, 26, who averages 11.71 points per game, plus a 2029 third. It comes out 557 ahead, 1,653 to 1,096, and the package adjustment is why: at face value the two sides are 1,816 and 1,647. PerryCock is fourth in points at 1,136.50, the projection gives it an 88% chance at the playoffs, and its own 2027 first belongs to Matty Ice, so it has no draft pick to protect by losing.
takes.10: Open for Business made this trade about two and a half hours before the McMillan deal and sold 11.71 points per game for three second-round picks. Those picks count for 1,096 after the package adjustment, down from 1,647, so it loses the deal by 557. Between the two trades it gave up 46.51 points per game on Monday. At 4-4 and seventh it projects to a playoff chance under 1%, and it now holds two firsts and two seconds in 2027.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Bad Bunny's Bush wins the A.J. Brown trade with degr

takes.4: Sleeper files this trade under Week 6, which is why the record above reads 4-1, but it went through on October 30, with Bad Bunny's Bush 6-1 and in first. It sent A.J. Brown, 29, to degr for Josh Jacobs, 28, and degr's 2027 second, a mid second by projection, and comes out 391 ahead, 1,871 to 1,480 (2,150 at face value before the package adjustment). Jacobs has scored in one game this season, 20.1 points, and Brown has 19.1 over three. At 7-1 it is second in points at 1,237.40, 52.70 behind Murrdawgs Massage Parlor in the $400 points race.
takes.12: degr was 2-5 and eleventh when this went through on October 30, not the 2-3 of the Week 6 tag above, and it is now 2-6 after five straight losses. It paid Josh Jacobs and its 2027 second for A.J. Brown, 29, and ends 391 behind in value. It owns two first-round picks, neither in 2027: its 2027 first went from Matty Ice to Open for Business on Monday, so a low Max PF would not earn degr anything next year.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Cheesehead10 and closed for business make an even swap of 2028 thirds

takes.3: Eight minutes after the Jameson Williams trade, Cheesehead10 took back Bijan al Gaib's 2028 third and sent ChrisUMD23's 2028 third instead. The model rates ChrisUMD23's pick as an early third, valued at 331, and Bijan al Gaib's as a late one at 275, so Cheesehead10 gives up 56, an even trade. It still owns four 2028 thirds.
takes.10: closed for business gains 56 in value by trading a late 2028 third for an early one. With the Williams trade, it ends up with Germie Bernard, Cheesehead10's 2028 second and ChrisUMD23's 2028 third for Jameson Williams. It now owns two 2028 seconds and one 2028 third.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Cheesehead10 and closed for business make an even trade for Jameson Williams

takes.3: Cheesehead10 is 3-4, eighth and one game behind sixth-place closed for business, and paid Germie Bernard, its own 2028 second and a 2028 third for Jameson Williams. Williams, 25, averages 14.28 points per game to Bernard's 9.8. The value is even, 1,595 for Williams against 1,645 for the package, which the package adjustment trims from 2,167 at face value. The extra points raise Cheesehead10's projected Max PF and move its own 2027 first from an average slot of 4.58 to 4.81, a small cost for a team that still holds seven first-round picks.
takes.10: closed for business is 4-3 and holds the sixth and last playoff spot, and it sold Jameson Williams for a 22-year-old receiver and two 2028 picks. It comes out 50 ahead in value but gives up 4.48 points per game in the swap of Williams for Bernard. Its roster value ranks 11th and it owns one first-round pick, in 2029, so the picks add to a thin cupboard. Eight minutes later it sent the 2028 third back to Cheesehead10 for a different one.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Cheesehead10 and degr make an even trade for Ollie Gordon II

takes.3: Cheesehead10 is rebuilding at 2-4, tenth in the standings, and paid its own 2027 second-round pick for Ollie Gordon II, a 22-year-old running back averaging 17.4 points over two games. It gained 158 in value, 1,130 to 972. The draft takes more than that back: Gordon's projected points raise Cheesehead10's Max PF, which costs 245 in value across the 2027 picks it owns and moves its own 2027 first from a projected average slot of 3.89 to 4.42. A low Max PF, not losses, is what earns 1.01, so this buy works against the race to the bottom, though Cheesehead10 still holds seven first-round picks and the league's most valuable roster.
takes.12: degr is 2-4, ninth and one game back of sixth, has lost three straight, and sold Ollie Gordon II for Cheesehead10's 2027 second. It gave up 158 in value and 17.4 points per game. The pick should come early in the round, since Cheesehead10's own first projects to an average slot of 4.42. degr owns no 2027 first-round pick and now holds three 2027 seconds.

tradeAnalysis.headline: PhilthyPhil wins the Jordan Mason trade with Cheesehead10

takes.3: Cheesehead10 is rebuilding at 2-4, in tenth place, and sold Jordan Mason and Ryan Flournoy for PhilthyPhil's 2027 second-round pick, taking back 729 in value for 896 and losing 167. The draft makes back part of that: losing 20.63 points per game lowers Cheesehead10's Max PF, which adds 55 in value to the 2027 picks it owns and moves its own 2027 first from a projected average slot of 3.82 to 3.67. A low Max PF, not losses, is what earns 1.01, and Cheesehead10 still holds seven first-round picks and the league's most valuable roster.
takes.8: PhilthyPhil is 5-1, second in the standings, and added Jordan Mason and Ryan Flournoy for a late 2027 second, a gain of 167 in value. Flournoy has 8.73 points per game over six games, and Mason has played one game, scoring 11.9. The pair adds up to 1,040 before the package adjustment and 896 after it, because neither is close to a star. PhilthyPhil has 868.05 points, fourth in the league and 74.95 behind Murrdawgs Massage Parlor in the $400 points race, and its own picks project late, with an average 2027 slot of 9.41.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor and closed for business make an even Jaylin Noel trade

takes.2: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor added Jaylin Noel, valued at 587, for a 2028 second valued at 507, close enough to call the deal even. Noel has 67.0 points in six games, 11.17 per game, which adds receiver depth for a 4-2 team in third place. Murrdawgs lead the league with 943.0 points, 33.2 ahead of PerryCock in the race for the $400 points prize, and still own four first-round picks.
takes.10: closed for business is 4-2 and in fourth, yet it sold a 24-year-old receiver averaging 11.17 points a game for a future second, coming up 80 short in value. Its roster ranked 11th in value before the deal and it owns one first-round pick, so the second adds to a thin draft stash. The same day it also spent $11 of FAAB on receiver Jordan Watkins.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Cheesehead10 wins the Luther Burden trade

takes.3: Cheesehead10 sold Luther Burden, 22, with 11.16 points per game, for closed for business's 2027 first and a 2028 second, and comes out 1,823 ahead in value, 30% of the deal. closed for business is 3-2, but it reaches the playoffs in only about 15% of the projections, so that first projects to an average slot of 4.29; record does not set the draft order, Max PF does. Selling Burden's points also lowers Cheesehead10's own projected Max PF, which moves its own 2027 first from an average slot of 2.77 to 2.52, worth about 173 more in the race to the bottom. It now owns seven first-round picks.
takes.11: ChrisUMD23 is 1-4 and last, and paid two picks for a 22-year-old receiver averaging 11.16 points per game, giving up 1,823 in value. ChrisUMD23 does not own a 2027 first-round pick, so a low Max PF earns it nothing next year and adding points costs it nothing in that draft. After the deal it owns two first-round picks, in 2028 and 2029, and the league's lowest roster value.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor win the Tony Pollard trade

takes.2: The 4-1 league leader added Tony Pollard, 29, for a 2028 third and came out 162 ahead in value. Pollard averages 8.74 points a game, depth at running back, Murrdawgs' weakest starting position (5th in the league by rest-of-season value). Murrdawgs lead the race for the $400 points prize with 806, 34 ahead of PhilthyPhil. They also own ChrisUMD23's 2027 first, and taking Pollard off that roster lowers ChrisUMD23's projected Max PF, worth about 42 to that pick.
takes.11: ChrisUMD23 is 1-4 and last, and it sold a 29-year-old running back for a future third, 162 short in value. The deal went through 25 seconds after it bought Jared Goff, so the day turned a back and a 2027 third into a quarterback and a 2028 third. ChrisUMD23 holds three first-round picks, one in each of the next three drafts, but not its own 2027 first.

tradeAnalysis.headline: ChrisUMD23 wins the Jared Goff trade with Cheesehead10

takes.3: Cheesehead10 sold Jared Goff, 32, and his 31.17 points per game for ChrisUMD23's 2027 third, coming up 365 short in value. Goff projects to outscore Jayden Daniels the rest of the way, so he counted toward Cheesehead10's projected Max PF, and Max PF sets the draft order for non-playoff teams. Without him, its own 2027 first moves from an average projected slot of 3.08 to 2.65, worth about 286, so the race to the bottom makes back most of the loss. Cheesehead10 still owns six first-round picks.
takes.11: ChrisUMD23 was 1-3 and 11th, one game out of sixth, when it added Goff for a 2027 third, and it came out 365 ahead in value. Goff joins Jalen Hurts (21.07 points per game) and Michael Penix at quarterback. ChrisUMD23 does not own its own 2027 first; Murrdawgs Massage Parlor does, so any points Goff adds push that pick later for Murrdawgs, not for ChrisUMD23.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor win the Rico Dowdle trade

takes.2: The 4-1 league leader added Rico Dowdle, valued at 350, for a 2029 third valued at 201, a gain of 149. Dowdle has 10.5 points in two games, 5.25 per game, so he is depth more than a difference-maker. Murrdawgs also lead the league with 806 points, 34 ahead of PhilthyPhil in the race for the $400 points prize, and still own four first-round picks.
takes.3: Cheesehead10 is rebuilding at 1-4 and sold a 28-year-old running back for a future pick, coming up 149 short in value. Running backs that age lose value quickly under the league's age curve, so moving him now fits the plan. Cheesehead10 still has the league's most valuable roster and six first-round picks, and its own 2027 first projects to an average slot of about 2.6.

tradeAnalysis.headline: degr wins the Jordan Love trade with Matty Ice

takes.1: Matty Ice sold Jordan Love (26.04 points per game) and Rashid Shaheed for a 2029 third and gave up 827 in value, 66% of the deal, after the package adjustment. The league's value model discounts quarterbacks, which makes the loss smaller than the market price suggests, but it is still a clear loss. The bigger effect is on the draft: Matty owns degr's 2027 first, and every point Love scores for degr raises degr's Max PF and pushes that pick later, about 50 in pick value by the draft projection. His own 2027 first still projects to 1.01.
takes.12: degr adds 31.7 points per game in Love and Shaheed for a 2029 third, a cheap price for a team chasing a playoff spot. degr's own 2027 first belongs to Matty Ice, so a playoff push costs degr nothing in next year's draft. degr owns two first-round picks, in 2028 and 2029.

tradeAnalysis.headline: closed for business wins the Jerry Jeudy trade

takes.3: Cheesehead10 turned Jerry Jeudy, 27, with 5.37 points per game over three games, into a 2029 third and came up 118 short in value, because a third-round pick three drafts out is worth little. The move still fits a rebuild that already holds six first-round picks and the league's most valuable roster.
takes.10: closed for business adds Jeudy for a pick valued at 211, a small bet on 5.37 points per game that comes out 118 ahead. The team owns one first-round pick and its roster value ranks 11th, so it is short on assets for bigger moves.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Cheesehead10 wins the Rebuild Bowl swap

takes.1: Matty Ice turned two receivers into a 2028 2nd and gave up 525 in value, 34% of the deal, after the package adjustment. He sold 13.9 combined points per game right after his first win of the season. With nine first-round picks from 2027 to 2029, it is a rebuild collecting more draft capital, but this one cost him value.
takes.3: Cheesehead10 bought two receivers with a pick it had owned for less than a day. Germie Bernard is 22, so the deal still fits a rebuild while adding some production. Counting picks, Cheesehead10 has the most valuable roster in the league.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Bad Bunny's Bush adds Woody Marks for the playoff push

takes.4: Bad Bunny's Bush was 3-1 and third when it made this deal, and it came out 276 ahead in value. Marks averages 8.66 points a game, which makes him running back depth for a contender. The price was a 2028 2nd, a pick that matters less to a team built to win this year.
takes.3: Cheesehead10 lost 276 in value on Marks after holding him for 11 days. Selling a back it was starting also lowered its projected Max PF, which moves its own 2027 first from an average slot of 2.80 to 2.65, worth about 92, so the race to the bottom gets back part of the loss. It moved the 2028 2nd to Matty Ice the next day for Bernard and Flournoy, so the pick was a stepping stone.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Bijan al Gaib wins the Amon-Ra St. Brown trade

takes.9: Bijan al Gaib paid with quantity and its last first-round pick, and got the best player in the deal. The league's package adjustment counts the extra pieces closed for business took back at less than face value, so Bijan comes out 3,982 ahead, 41% of the deal. It took on 38.7 points per game and sent out 23.4. At 2-2 and seventh when the deal happened, this was a buy for the playoff push, and Bijan al Gaib is now 3-2 with three straight wins.
takes.10: closed for business was 3-1 and fourth when it sold its best receiver for eight assets, including Bijan al Gaib's 2029 1st and 2nd. Those pieces add up to about as much as Amon-Ra St. Brown at face value, but eight roster spots of smaller assets do not equal one star, and after the package adjustment the deal comes out 3,982 against it. It lost its first game after the sale by 92.15 points.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Bijan al Gaib wins the Washington-for-McConkey swap

takes.3: Cheesehead10 traded the more productive receiver, 16.7 points a game, for one averaging 9.07, plus a 2028 3rd, and comes out 1,333 behind. Parker Washington is valued well above Ladd McConkey, and the 3rd counts for less as an add-on to the lesser player. Taking back the less productive receiver does lower its projected Max PF, which moves its own 2027 first from an average slot of 2.90 to 2.65, worth about 159 in the race to the bottom. McConkey scored 0.0 on Cheesehead10's bench in Week 5.
takes.9: Bijan al Gaib got the better receiver for a lesser one plus a late pick, which suits a team chasing a playoff spot. Parker Washington scored 32.4 in his first game for them.

tradeAnalysis.headline: PhilthyPhil sells Woody Marks for a 2nd

takes.8: PhilthyPhil was 3-0 and second when it moved Marks for a 2028 2nd. It gave up 207 in value and a running back averaging 8.66 a game. It is 4-1 with the league's second-most points, so it has not missed him.
takes.3: Cheesehead10 gained 207 in value and started Marks in Weeks 4 and 5, for 8.2 and 12.5 points. Then it traded him to Bad Bunny's Bush.

tradeAnalysis.headline: Cheesehead10 gets Jordan Mason for a 3rd

takes.3: Cheesehead10 added 390 in value for a 2029 3rd. Adding a running back works against the race to the bottom, though: the extra projected points push its own 2027 first from an average slot of 2.52 to 2.65, about 82 in pick value. Mason has scored in one game this season (11.9) and put up a zero on the bench in Week 4.
takes.9: Bijan al Gaib cleared a roster spot and got a 2029 3rd. A week later that pick went to closed for business as part of the Amon-Ra St. Brown trade.

5.dek: The last unbeaten team loses on Monday night with the winning lineup on its bench. Amon-Ra's Dynasty sells Amon-Ra and closes for business. Matty Ice finally wins a game, then sells two of the players who won it.

stories.h: Murrdawgs lose a 69-point Monday lead
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor finished Sunday ahead of Bad Bunny's Bush 183.60–114.50 with nobody left to play. Bad Bunny's Bush had Josh Allen and Puka Nacua in Bills–Rams on Monday night and needed 69.1 points from them. The game went to overtime, Allen scored 36.6, Nacua scored 39.7, and Bad Bunny's Bush won 190.80–183.60. That 183.60 is the highest losing score of the season. The Murrdawgs could have avoided all of it. Blake Corum scored 16.2 on their bench in that same Monday game while RJ Harvey scored 0.7 at flex. With Corum in, they win by 8.3. The league now has three 4-1 teams, and the Murrdawgs still lead in points for (806.00).

stories.h: Amon-Ra's Dynasty is now "closed for business"
stories.body: Last week NotGomes was 3-1 on the league's softest schedule. This week he sent Amon-Ra St. Brown, T.J. Hockenson and J.K. Dobbins to Bijan al Gaib for Zach Charbonnet, Michael Wilson, Rome Odunze, Ja'Kobi Lane and Bijan al Gaib's 2029 1st, 2nd and 3rd. Then he renamed the team "closed for business." The first game after the sale was a 192.35–100.20 loss to PhilthyPhil, the biggest margin of the week. The new arrivals scored 12.35 combined, with Charbonnet and Lane both at 0.0 on the bench.

stories.h: Bijan al Gaib has no first-round picks left
stories.body: Bijan al Gaib is the most all-in team in the league. After this week's trades they own zero first-round picks from 2027 through 2029. They also bought Parker Washington from Cheesehead10 for Ladd McConkey and a 2028 3rd. Washington scored 32.4 in London on Sunday and St. Brown added 12.9 in his debut. Bijan al Gaib has won three straight and put up 161.45 this week. Cheesehead10 got a 0.0 from McConkey on its bench.

stories.h: Matty Ice wins, then sells
stories.body: Matty Ice scored a season-high 140.05 and beat PerryCock for his first win. His lineup was within 6.5 points of perfect, the closest in the league for the second straight week. Then he traded two of his starters, Ryan Flournoy (12.0) and Germie Bernard (14.4), to Cheesehead10 for a 2028 2nd. He also dropped George Holani, Najee Harris and Malik Davis. Matty now holds nine first-round picks from 2027 to 2029. Cheesehead10 holds six. They are both 1-4 and sit 10th and 11th in points for.

stories.h: Woody Marks has seen the whole league
stories.body: Woody Marks went from ChrisUMD23 to PhilthyPhil in August. PhilthyPhil sent him to Cheesehead10 in Week 4 for a 2028 2nd. He started for Cheesehead10 this week and scored 12.5. Then Cheesehead10 flipped him to Bad Bunny's Bush for Bad Bunny's 2028 2nd, and sent that pick to Matty Ice for Flournoy and Bernard. Marks is on his fourth team since August.

stories.h: Luck check: PerryCock and CeeDeez Nutz
stories.body: PerryCock is 4th in points for (729.65) and 1-4. Opponents have scored 786.25 against them, the most in the league. If every team played every other team each week, PerryCock would be 36-19. CeeDeez Nutz is the opposite. They are 3-2 with the league's lowest points against (516.25) and an all-play record of 26-29. They also benched Drake Maye for the second week in a row. He scored 34.85 on the bench in Week 4 and 53.2 this week. That 53.2 is the highest score by any player this season.

stories.h: 215 points on the benches, one result changed
stories.body: The league left 215.05 points on its benches this week. Only one of those decisions changed a result: Murrdawgs starting RJ Harvey over Blake Corum. The three highest scores of the season all came this week: PhilthyPhil (192.35), Bad Bunny's Bush (190.80) and Murrdawgs (183.60).

games.h: Monday Night Heist
t: Murrdawgs led 99.4–94.7 after the early games and 160.6–114.5 after the late games. Derrick Henry's 23.0 on Sunday night made it 183.6–114.5. Every Murrdawgs starter was done. Bad Bunny's Bush needed 69.1 points from Josh Allen and Puka Nacua in Bills–Rams. They got 76.3 in an overtime game, and the unbeaten streak was over.

Murrdawgs did plenty right. Joe Burrow (34.5), Isaiah Likely (32.4), Mike Evans (28.3), Garrett Wilson (25.4) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (24.8) all went off. The problem was flex. RJ Harvey started and scored 0.7. Blake Corum scored 16.2 on the bench, and he was playing in the Monday game. Their best lineup scored 199.4.

Bad Bunny's Bush got 38.8 from Jaylen Warren and 20.6 from Braelon Allen on Sunday. Tee Higgins (4.2) and Romeo Doubs (2.6) did little. Matthew Stafford threw for 383 yards in the Monday game and scored 39.15 on their bench, 2.55 more than the starter.
games.v: Game of the week. A 69-point Monday deficit erased by two players.

games.h: Ugly Win, Uglier Loss
t: ChrisUMD23 led 54.0–43.7 after the early games. Jalen Hurts (17.2) and Hunter Henry (13.4) were the only starters who did much. Then Jacoby Brissett scored 34.2 in Lions–Cardinals and CeeDeez Nutz went ahead 80.1–58.8. Chris had nobody left. Mark Andrews and Tyler Higbee, a $0 waiver pickup who started at flex, added 18.1 more.

Chris's four running back starters scored 8.9 combined. Saquon Barkley scored 0.0, David Montgomery 1.1 and Alvin Kamara 2.6. Michael Penix scored 18.8 on the bench. Even his best lineup (81.7) loses.
CeeDeez Nutz won with 98.2 while Drake Maye scored 53.2 on the bench. CeeDee Lamb scored 2.9 on Thursday.
games.v: A small comeback in a bad game. Two teams combined for 157 points.

games.h: Matty Gets One
t: Matty Ice led 12.0–5.5 after Thursday and 130.65–66.0 after the early games. Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and scored 34.95, Malik Nabers had 121 yards and 31.1, and Brock Bowers had 110 yards and 25.0. Matty's running backs, Holani and Sanders, combined for 7.4.

PerryCock scored 53.25 after the early games, including James Cook's 24.8 on Monday, and fell short by 20.8. Ja'Marr Chase (19.7) and Justin Jefferson (18.8) were fine. Bo Nix scored 11.15. Kyle Pitts scored 15.2 on the bench while Cade Otton started for 5.5. Their best lineup (128.95) still loses.
Matty left 6.5 points on his bench, the fewest in the league. After the game he traded Flournoy and Bernard, who had combined for 26.4 in this game.
games.v: Decided by Sunday afternoon. Matty's first win of the year.

games.h: Season High
t: Bucky Irving ran for 165 yards on Thursday and gave PhilthyPhil a 33.5–0 head start. Christian Watson (34.3, 143 yards) and C.J. Stroud (25.55) pushed it to 126.85–61.55 after the early games. Jahmyr Gibbs added 39.7 in the late window and Davante Adams 22.1 on Monday.

closed for business got 30.35 from Aaron Rodgers and 21.4 from Tyler Warren. Brian Thomas scored 0.0 in the lineup, and MarShawn Lloyd (16.7) and Jaylin Noel (15.2) sat on the bench. The new players from the Amon-Ra trade, Michael Wilson and Rome Odunze, scored 7.35 and 5.0.
PhilthyPhil started Dalton Kincaid (3.7) over Brenton Strange (13.8) for the second week in a row. At 192.35, it didn't matter.
games.v: Over on Thursday. The biggest margin of the week (92.15).

games.h: Steady Beats Nothing
t: Dak Prescott threw for 316 yards on Thursday and Geno-Cide led 19.8–0. It was 74.2–29.9 after the early games. Jared Goff's 37.65 in the late window got Cheesehead10 within 21, and Drake London's 20.8 on Sunday night got them within 14.85. Kyren Williams scored 19.6 on Monday to finish it.
Geno-Cide had no huge game. Trey McBride (21.6), Aaron Jones (20.7, 113 rushing yards), Prescott (19.8) and Williams (19.6) did the work.

Cheesehead10 left 29.3 on the bench. Emeka Egbuka scored 17.2 on Thursday on the bench while Carnell Tate (1.6) and Tre' Harris (3.6) started. Chig Okonkwo (10.0) sat behind Colston Loveland (3.9). Their best lineup (124.85) still loses.
games.v: Geno-Cide led at every checkpoint. Not much drama.

games.h: Over on Thursday
t: Bijan al Gaib had three Cowboys in the Thursday game and got 49.1 out of them. George Pickens had 130 yards and 30.0 points. Trevor Lawrence (31.05) and Parker Washington (32.4, 124 yards) added 63.45 from the London game on Sunday morning.

Amon-Ra St. Brown scored 12.9 in his first game for Bijan al Gaib. J.K. Dobbins scored 15.4 on the bench and T.J. Hockenson 1.7.
games.v: Boring. Decided before most people woke up on Sunday.

Maye threw for 374 yards and scored 53.2, the best game by any player this season, on the bench. That makes 88.05 benched Maye points in two weeks.

awards.a: The Unbeaten Streak Was on the Bench
awards.p: RJ Harvey scored 0.7 at flex. Blake Corum scored 16.2 on the bench, in the Monday game that beat them. The swap wins by 8.3.
First win of the year, 140.05 points. Then he traded two starters for a 2028 2nd and cut three running backs. The front office will not tolerate this kind of winning.
Renamed the team, sold Amon-Ra, then lost by the week's biggest margin. Brian Thomas scored 0.0 in the lineup. The sign on the door is accurate.
The team named after CeeDee Lamb got 2.9 from him on Thursday. George Pickens had 130 receiving yards in the same game.

Week's low and the second-lowest score of the season. Four running back starters (Pollard, Montgomery, Kamara, Barkley) combined for 8.9. Saquon Barkley scored 0.0.
4th in points, most points against, and a 36-19 all-play record. They scored 119.25 this week and ran into Matty Ice's best game of the year.

4.dek: An unbeaten team survives on a backup quarterback, the rebuilders keep losing on schedule, and one manager left the winning lineup on his bench.

stories.h: Murrdawgs are 4-0, and Monday night is the reason
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor is the league's last unbeaten team, but this was the closest call yet. After Sunday they trailed Matty Ice 102.15–89.20, and every Matty starter was finished. Tyler Shough needed 13 points on Monday night. He put up 20.80, and the Murrdawgs escaped by 7.85. Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards and scored 30.00 on their bench all weekend. Their 110.00 was a season low by 44 points, and they still lead the league in points for (622.40).

stories.h: The Rebuild Bowl is going as planned
stories.body: Matty Ice and Cheesehead10 were on one side of 18 and 24 of the league's 40 trades, plenty of them with each other. Between them they now hold nine extra future first-round picks (Matty +6, Cheesehead +3, 2027–29). They are also a combined 1-7 and sit 10th and 12th in points. The rebuild is working exactly as designed, if the design was "lose a lot." Matty also owns the season's lowest single score (49.25 in Week 2).

stories.h: PerryCock: second in points, 1-3 in the standings
stories.body: No one has had worse luck. PerryCock has scored 610.40 (2nd) and given up 646.20, the most in the league. In Week 3 they went all-in, sending Chris Godwin, Adonai Mitchell, a 2027 2nd, a 2028 1st and a 2029 3rd to ChrisUMD23 for Christian McCaffrey. CMC has delivered 21.6 and 16.0. This week Ja'Marr Chase scored 5.7 in a game where his quarterback threw for 428 yards, while Tee Higgins put 28.7 on them from the other side.

stories.h: Amon-Ra's Dynasty is 3-1 on schedule luck
stories.body: Amon-Ra's Dynasty is 9th in points for (483.45) but tied for second in the standings, because opponents have scored a league-low 367.30 against them. That is 75 points fewer than any other team. They have also traded away three more future firsts than they've received, so this is a team that is all-in and getting help from the schedule.

stories.h: The Ollie Gordon waiver saga
stories.body: In Week 2, Amon-Ra's Dynasty dropped Ollie Gordon II and spent $103 of FAAB on Ted Hurst. Hurst has never made their starting lineup (4.7, 11.0, 4.5). A week later degr spent $158 on Gordon. On Sunday, Gordon ran for 100 yards and scored 20.0 on degr's bench. Both teams paid a lot of money for a backup.

stories.h: The league left 342 points on its benches
stories.body: The twelve teams left 341.6 points on their benches in Week 4. Only one of those decisions changed a result (see PhilthyPhil, below). The only manager to set a near-perfect lineup, within 0.1 of his best possible score, was Matty Ice, and he lost anyway.

games.h: Monday Night Shough
t: Matty Ice led 58.6–40.3 after the early games and 102.15–89.20 when Sunday ended. All nine of his starters were finished. Murrdawgs had one player left, Tyler Shough, who needed 13 points. He scored 20.8 and the unbeaten streak survived.

Malik Nabers (25.2), Brock Bowers (20.6) and Jordan Love (19.05) carried Matty. His three running backs, Holani, Sanders and Najee Harris, combined for 9.6. His bench had four IR players and nothing that would have helped. The lineup was within 0.1 of perfect.
Murrdawgs left 29 points on the bench, mostly Joe Burrow's 30 and Sam Darnold's 19. Starting Shough over both was a bad call that happened to work out.
games.v: Best game of the week. Matty lost with a perfect lineup to a backup QB on Monday night.

games.h: The Sunday Night Swing
t: ChrisUMD23 led 82.65–68.6 after the late games and had no one left. Amon-Ra's Dynasty had three players in the Lions–Panthers game on Sunday night. Tetairoa McMillan (47.2), Jameson Williams (18.2) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (15.5) scored 80.9 in that one game. A 14-point deficit became a 67-point win.

Chris's lineup had problems. Kenyon Sadiq scored 0.0 at tight end while Mike Gesicki (13.0) and Hunter Henry (11.2) sat. Saquon Barkley scored 2.0 at flex while Alvin Kamara put up 22.8 on the bench. Even his best lineup (125.65) would have lost.
Amon-Ra also left 44 points on the bench, including T.J. Hockenson (26.9) and Keon Coleman (25.6). Winning by 67 hides a lot.
games.v: A real comeback that ended as a blowout. Chris led for most of the weekend.

games.h: Bijan Saves Bijan al Gaib
t: Bijan al Gaib led 100.5–65.9 after Sunday afternoon. Jared Goff threw for 412 yards on Sunday night and scored 26.6, which cut the lead to 8. Both teams went into Monday night with players in Falcons–Saints.

The team named after Bijan Robinson won because of Bijan Robinson. He ran for 145 yards and scored 29.7. Cheesehead's Drake London (14.6) and Kendre Miller (1.9) could not keep up. Cheesehead started Miller over Tyler Allgeier, who scored 12.9 on the bench.

Bijan al Gaib was also sloppy. They started Ladd McConkey for a zero and benched Emanuel Wilson's 27.0, leaving 39.7 points on the bench. Cheesehead traded picks for Woody Marks and Jordan Mason this week. Marks scored 8.2 in his first start for them. Mason scored 0 on the bench.
games.v: Close going into Monday night. Robinson ended it.

games.h: The One That Got Away
t: DylanDaKing got 21.6 from Quinshon Judkins on Thursday and had 125.7 by the end of the early games. CeeDee Lamb (43.3, 189 yards) and Chuba Hubbard (27.9 on Sunday night) did most of the work.

The final score looks one-sided, but PhilthyPhil's best possible lineup scored 154.45. That would have beaten Dylan by 0.90. Brian Robinson (25.7), Brenton Strange (16.5) and Denzel Boston (12.9) sat on the bench while Rashee Rice (0.0), Dalton Kincaid (1.7) and Bucky Irving (6.1) started.
Dylan made a bad call too. He benched Drake Maye's 34.85 to start Kyler Murray (13.95), but Lamb made up for it.
games.v: The worst lineup decision of the week. It was the only one that changed a result.

games.h: Over by 1 p.m.
t: Bad Bunny's Bush led 140.7–32.9 when the early games ended. PerryCock then scored 104.8 in the late, Sunday night and Monday night games. Kenneth Walker scored 32.9, Bryce Young 30.75 and Chris Olave 21.6. That made the 25-point final margin look closer than the game was.

Bad Bunny's Bush got big games from everyone. Puka Nacua (29.7), Tee Higgins (28.7), Josh Allen (23.05), Jonathan Taylor (22.7) and Sam LaPorta (22.4) all scored 20+, and Romeo Doubs added 23.8 on the bench.
PerryCock's stars were the problem. Ja'Marr Chase scored 5.7, Travis Kelce 3.5 and Josh Downs 4.6. Christian McCaffrey, the big Week 3 trade, added 16.0.
games.v: Decided early. PerryCock scored the rest of the way, but the game was already over.

games.h: Decided by 4 p.m.
t: Geno-Cide Smith scored 152.6 in the early games alone. Kyren Williams (36.7), Nico Collins (32.8), Zay Flowers (27.8) and Dak Prescott (25.45) all went off at once. degr gained ground in the late games and got within 28.8, but had only Devaughn Vele left for Monday night.
degr made one good call: Kyle Monangai scored 30.0 at flex after a 146-yard day. Ollie Gordon's 20.0 on the bench was only 1.6 more than the starter he sat behind, so it didn't matter much.
Geno-Cide started Terry McLaurin for a zero and Dalton Schultz for 2.9, with DK Metcalf (18.5) and Roman Wilson (16.4) on the bench. They scored the week's high anyway.
games.v: Boring. It was over by mid-afternoon Sunday.

awards.p: 47.2 points and 192 yards on Sunday night. He erased a 14-point deficit almost by himself and turned it into a 67-point win.
They had 152.6 on the board before the 4 p.m. games kicked off. Everyone else spent Sunday afternoon trying to catch up.
They benched a 30-point Joe Burrow, started Tyler Shough, needed 13 on Monday night and got 20.8. Undefeated teams win ugly sometimes.
His best possible lineup scored 154.45. He lost 153.55–102.05. Brian Robinson (25.7) and Brenton Strange (16.5) watched from the bench while Rashee Rice put up a zero.
He set a perfect lineup and still lost. His three running back slots combined for 9.6 points. The front office thanks him for protecting the draft pick.
They're 3-1 despite being 9th in points, and their opponents have averaged 91.8 a week. They should play the lottery.
$261 of FAAB bought one 20-point game, on a bench, and one receiver who has never been started.
Terry McLaurin (Geno-Cide), Ladd McConkey (Bijan al Gaib), Rashee Rice (PhilthyPhil) and Kenyon Sadiq (ChrisUMD23) all scored 0.0 in starting lineups. Check the injury report before kickoff.
Week's low score. They led after the late games, then Sunday night happened. Saquon Barkley scored 2.0 in a flex spot while Alvin Kamara put up 22.8 on the bench.
Burrow threw for 428 yards and Chase scored 5.7. Higgins scored 28.7 against them. Some weeks fantasy football is just mean.

6.dek: Murrdawgs lose on Monday night for the second week in a row, this time to Cheesehead10. PerryCock scores 180 and stays 2-4. Matty Ice scores 58.0, and the players Matty sold score 79.5 for other teams.

stories.h: Murrdawgs lose on Monday night again
stories.body: Last week Murrdawgs Massage Parlor lost a 69.1-point Monday lead. This week the lead was 5.0 and it went the same way. Cheesehead10 had Jayden Daniels (30.0) and Rachaad White (15.7) in Commanders–49ers. Murrdawgs had Mike Evans (12.4) and George Kittle (17.9) in the same game. Cheesehead10 won 147.40–137.00. Murrdawgs left 33.7 points on the bench, including Stefon Diggs (16.4), RJ Harvey (14.6) and Blake Corum (14.0), while Cam Skattebo scored 0.0 in the lineup. Their best lineup scored 170.7. Last week they started Harvey over Corum and lost. This week they benched both. Murrdawgs were 4-0 two weeks ago and are now 4-2 and third.

stories.h: Matty Ice's old players outscore Matty Ice
stories.body: Matty Ice scored 58.0 and lost to closed for business 76.05–58.00. It is the second-lowest score of the season, behind Matty Ice's own 49.25 in Week 2. Four starters scored 0.0: Fernando Mendoza, Adam Randall, Raheim Sanders and Efton Chism. Malik Nabers scored 30.5, more than half the team total. The four players Matty traded away in the last two deals scored 79.5 for their new teams. Germie Bernard (25.7) and Ryan Flournoy (17.0) went to Cheesehead10. Jordan Love (25.0) and Rashid Shaheed (11.8) went to degr. Matty Ice is 1-5, last in points for (549.0), and has the lowest Maximum Points For by 144.25. The draft projection puts Matty's own first at 1.01 in essentially every simulation.

stories.h: closed for business is 4-2 on the softest path in the league
stories.body: closed for business won with 76.05, the lowest winning score of the season. They are 4-2 and fourth in the standings while ranking ninth in points for (659.7). Opponents have scored 617.65 against them, the fewest in the league, and their all-play record is 22-44. They also benched Jaylin Noel (22.7) and Jerry Jeudy (10.9) and started Tyler Warren and Brian Thomas, who both scored 0.0. The record has not convinced the projection. closed for business reaches the playoffs in about 10% of simulations. Their 2027 first belongs to Cheesehead10, and it projects to an average slot of 3.31.

stories.h: PerryCock scores 180.15 and is still 2-4
stories.body: PerryCock beat degr 180.15–113.30, the week's high score and the fourth-highest of the season. Christian McCaffrey (30.7), Kenneth Walker (29.9), Bryce Young (26.65), James Cook (24.3) and Kyle Pitts (23.0) all cleared 23 points. PerryCock is second in points for (909.8), has allowed the most points (899.55) and has a 47-19 all-play record. The win also closed the $400 points race to 33.2: Murrdawgs 943.0, PerryCock 909.8, Bad Bunny's Bush 883.6. The rules add a twist. A points leader who does not reach the championship game picks 1.10.

stories.h: Cheesehead10 keeps selling, ChrisUMD23 keeps buying
stories.body: Cheesehead10 sold Rico Dowdle to Murrdawgs for a 2029 3rd and Luther Burden to ChrisUMD23 for closed for business's 2027 1st and ChrisUMD23's 2028 2nd. Cheesehead10 now owns seven first-round picks and the league's most valuable roster. ChrisUMD23 has been buying, adding Jared Goff and then Burden, even though Murrdawgs own ChrisUMD23's 2027 first. Burden scored 17.5 in his debut and ChrisUMD23 beat Bijan al Gaib 134.55–110.40. Dowdle scored 7.9 on the Murrdawgs bench against Cheesehead10.

stories.h: Three results were decided on the bench
stories.body: The league left 190.85 points on its benches, and three losers would have won with their best lineup. Murrdawgs (170.7 possible) lost by 10.4. CeeDeez Nutz (154.05 possible) lost to Bad Bunny's Bush by 5.5 while DeMario Douglas (19.6) and Tyrone Tracy (18.5) sat. Geno-Cide Smith (99.5 possible) lost to PhilthyPhil by 3.85 with Juwan Johnson at 0.0 in the lineup and Dalton Schultz at 7.3 on the bench. Bad Bunny's Bush and PhilthyPhil both moved to 5-1.

stories.h: Bijan al Gaib wastes the week's best game
stories.body: Trevor Lawrence scored 40.4, the top score of the week, and Bijan al Gaib still lost by 24.15. Bijan Robinson scored 7.3 and Courtland Sutton 3.9. Bijan al Gaib is the league's most all-in team, with no first-round picks from 2027 through 2029, and is now 3-3.

games.h: Monday Night Heist, Part Two
t: Murrdawgs led 27.4–0 after Thursday on Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 27.4. They still led 106.7–93.2 after the early games and 106.7–101.7 going into Monday night. Both teams had two starters in Commanders–49ers. Cheesehead10 got 45.7 from them and Murrdawgs got 30.3, and Cheesehead10 won by 10.4.

Jayden Daniels scored 30.0 and Rachaad White 15.7 on Monday. Germie Bernard, acquired from Matty Ice last week, scored 25.7 at flex. Carnell Tate (19.0), Colston Loveland (18.5) and Emeka Egbuka (17.8) did the rest. Cheesehead10 still left 29.6 on the bench: Omar Cooper (24.3), Ryan Flournoy (17.0) and Michael Mayer (16.5), who Murrdawgs had dropped earlier in the week. Ladd McConkey scored 2.7 at flex.

Tyler Shough scored 34.4 and Isaiah Likely 23.9. Cam Skattebo scored 0.0, Derrick Henry 5.0 and new arrival Tony Pollard 7.6. Stefon Diggs (16.4), RJ Harvey (14.6) and Blake Corum (14.0) were on the bench, along with waiver pickups Kendrick Bourne (9.7) and Corey Kiner (5.7). Their best lineup scored 170.7 and would have won by 23.3.
games.v: Game of the week. Murrdawgs have now lost two straight on Monday night.

games.h: Bad Bunny's Bush holds off a prime-time rally
t: Bad Bunny's Bush led by 3.55 after the early games and by 38.2 after the late games, with every starter finished. CeeDeez Nutz got 24.7 from CeeDee Lamb and Tucker Kraft on Sunday night and 8.0 from Antonio Williams on Monday. That cut it to 5.5.
D'Andre Swift scored 23.0 at flex, Josh Allen 24.85 and Jonathan Taylor 21.1. Darren Waller scored 0.0 at tight end. Matthew Stafford scored 23.1 on the bench, 1.75 less than Allen.

Drake Maye was finally in the lineup and scored 32.15. The trouble was the tight ends. CeeDeez started three of them, and Mark Andrews (1.4), Tyler Higbee (4.2) and Kraft combined for 14.3. DeMario Douglas (19.6) and Tyrone Tracy (18.5) were on the bench. Their best lineup scored 154.05 and would have won.
games.v: Bad Bunny's Bush is 5-1 and won its fourth straight because CeeDeez started tight ends.

games.h: PhilthyPhil wins with Stroud on the bench
t: PhilthyPhil led 68.95–43.9 after the early games, and Geno-Cide Smith spent the rest of the week chasing. The lead was 13.75 after the late games and 7.55 after Sunday night. Terry McLaurin's 3.7 on Monday left Geno-Cide 3.85 short.

Bhayshul Tuten scored 24.7 and Caleb Williams 23.55. C.J. Stroud scored 34.1 on the bench, the best bench score of the week. Denzel Boston (2.5) and Harold Fannin (1.9) did little. Their best lineup scored 111.8.

Juwan Johnson scored 0.0 at flex while Dalton Schultz scored 7.3 on the bench. That swap alone wins the game by 3.45. DK Metcalf scored 20.3 and Dak Prescott 15.6. Najee Harris, a $6 waiver claim this week, scored 0.2 on the bench.
games.v: Close and sloppy. One tight end swap would have flipped it.

games.h: ChrisUMD23 beats the all-in team
t: Bijan al Gaib led 22.7–6.4 after Thursday on J.K. Dobbins and Courtland Sutton. ChrisUMD23 took over in the early games and led by 53.75 after the late games. Bijan al Gaib's Sunday night Cowboys cut that to 24.15.

Michael Penix scored 31.35, Tre Tucker 26.7 and Luther Burden 17.5 in his first game for the team. Alvin Kamara added 14.9 and Hunter Henry 14.8. ChrisUMD23's lineup was within 3.5 points of its best.
Trevor Lawrence scored 40.4, the top score of the week. Bijan Robinson scored 7.3, Jake Ferguson 3.3 and Sutton 3.9. Their best lineup scored 114.4, which still loses by 20.15.
games.v: A 1-4 team beat a 3-2 contender, and the lineup had nothing to do with it.

games.h: PerryCock puts up 180
t: degr led 4.6–0 after AJ Barner on Thursday. PerryCock led by 34.85 after the early games and by 82.55 after the late games. Christian McCaffrey's 30.7 on Monday made the final margin 66.85.
Kenneth Walker scored 29.9 at flex, Bryce Young 26.65, James Cook 24.3 and Kyle Pitts 23.0. Dameon Pierce scored 15.0 on the bench, and the lineup was within 7.0 of perfect.

Matthew Golden scored 24.4 and Brock Purdy 22.0. Jordan Love, acquired from Matty Ice, scored 25.0 on the bench, and Travis Hunter 15.9. Their best lineup scored 132.2, which still loses by 47.95. degr has lost three straight.
games.v: Over by Sunday afternoon.

games.h: The bottom of the scoreboard
t: Matty Ice led 47.0–44.05 after the early games, almost all of it from Malik Nabers. closed for business got 31.0 in the late games from Keon Coleman, Omarion Hampton and Michael Wilson, while Matty got 11.0 from Brock Bowers. Final: 76.05–58.00.

Aaron Rodgers scored 22.55, Keon Coleman 15.9 and Tetairoa McMillan 14.6. Tyler Warren and Brian Thomas both scored 0.0 in the lineup while Jaylin Noel scored 22.7 on the bench. Their best lineup scored 105.55.

Nabers scored 30.5 and Bowers 11.0. Fernando Mendoza, Adam Randall, Raheim Sanders and Efton Chism all scored 0.0. Nobody on the bench scored a point, so this was Matty Ice's best possible lineup. It still loses by 18.05.
games.v: Boring. The two lowest scores of the week.

Five starters over 23 points and the fourth-highest score of the season. They are 2-4.
The week's best bench score, 10.55 more than the starter. PhilthyPhil won by 3.85 anyway and is 5-1.
Zero points left on the bench, the most efficient lineup in the league for the third straight week. Four starters scored 0.0.

7.dek: Dak Prescott drops 31.4 on Monday night and Geno-Cide Smith loses the closest game of the season anyway, for the second week in a row. Murrdawgs finally hold a Monday lead, and Matty Ice scores 53.8 to own the three worst games of 2026.

stories.h: Geno-Cide Smith has lost the two closest games of the season, back to back
stories.body: Week 6: lost to PhilthyPhil by 3.85. Week 7: lost to ChrisUMD23 by 2.75, the new closest game of the year. Those are the top two on the list, and Geno-Cide Smith is on the wrong end of both. Dak Prescott put up 31.4 on Monday night to cut a 19.05-point hole down to nothing, and it still came up a field goal short because Saquon Barkley gave ChrisUMD23 15.1 in the same game. The best lineup (142.1) wins this one, and so does a normal Nico Collins game (2.6 on a 17.1 projection). Geno-Cide went from fifth to seventh and from 63% to 41% to make the playoffs. Willy, at some point you have to start beating people by 40 just to be safe.

stories.h: The Monday curse is dead, and Murrdawgs own the $400 race
stories.body: Two straight weeks Murrdawgs Massage Parlor blew a Monday night lead. This week they took a 30.3-point lead into Monday with zero players left and let degr try to get 30.3 out of Dallas Goedert. Goedert scored 9.8. Curse lifted, technically. The bigger news is the points race: Murrdawgs are at 1,101.9, Bad Bunny's Bush is 65.85 back at 1,036.05, and PerryCock is 88.75 back at 1,013.15. A week ago the lead over second place was 33.2. One catch from the rulebook: if the regular-season points leader does not reach the championship game, that team picks 1.10. The $400 comes with homework.

stories.h: Matty Ice went 1-6, and also went 3-1
stories.body: Matty Ice owns five 2027 first-round picks: Matty's own, plus PerryCock's, PhilthyPhil's, Bijan al Gaib's and degr's. That means Matty's real Sunday was rooting against four other teams, and three of them lost. PerryCock fell to 2-5, PhilthyPhil lost by 51.6, and degr dropped a fourth straight to sit 2-5 with a 19% shot at the playoffs. Only Bijan al Gaib let Matty down. Meanwhile Matty's own pick is the 1.01 in every simulation, because non-playoff teams draft by reverse Maximum Points For and Matty's Max PF (642.3) is 234.7 below anyone else's. The roster is a disaster. The draft capital is having a career year.

stories.h: Cheesehead10 is rebuilding so hard it keeps winning
stories.body: Cheesehead10 owns seven first-round picks and the most valuable roster in the league by Dynasty Daddy, and the tier label says "Rebuild with assets." This week the rebuild sold Ryan Flournoy and Jordan Mason to PhilthyPhil for a 2027 second, started a $0 waiver pickup (Zonovan Knight), started Kirk Cousins at quarterback for 27.35, beat the league's top-rated contender lineup, and then cut Cousins. After the games it flipped its own 2027 second to degr for Ollie Gordon II. Two straight wins, 3-4, and playoff odds up from 10% to 25%. Wonderman, pick a lane. Or don't. It's working.

stories.h: PhilthyPhil keeps benching the wrong quarterback
stories.body: Last week Phil started Caleb Williams and left C.J. Stroud's 34.1 on the bench. This week Phil went with Stroud (22.05, projected 23.4) and Caleb Williams scored 31.2 on the bench (projected 23.2). This week the projections were 0.2 apart, so call it a coin flip, and Phil has now lost the flip twice. Phil had company: the three best bench scores of the week were all quarterbacks (Williams 31.2, Bo Nix 30.5, Michael Penix Jr. 28.55), the league left 217.3 points on its benches, and degr, PerryCock and Geno-Cide Smith all would have won with their best lineup.

stories.h: PerryCock and closed for business are living in opposite universes
stories.body: PerryCock is third in points for (1,013.15), has allowed the most points in the league (1,025.9), owns a 49-28 all-play record, and is 2-5 in tenth place. closed for business is tenth in points for (747.8), has a 23-54 all-play record, and is 4-3 in sixth. The simulation still has PerryCock making the playoffs 72% of the time and closed for business 4%. One of these teams is going to be very mad in December. The math says it's NotGomes.

games.h: Dak Drops 31.4 on Monday Night, Geno-Cide Smith Loses by a Field Goal Anyway
t: Geno-Cide Smith has now lost the two closest games of the 2026 season in consecutive weeks. Last week it was 3.85 to PhilthyPhil. This week it was 136.05 to 133.30 against ChrisUMD23, and this one had a Monday night ending that will live in the group chat for a while.

ChrisUMD23 jumped out 39.8 to nothing on Thursday with Luther Burden (25.7) and Hunter Henry (14.1) in Patriots–Bears. Zay Flowers (29.7) dragged Geno-Cide back within 3.0 after the early games, then Tre Tucker went for 23.3 on a 9.1 projection and Jared Goff added 27.05, and Geno-Cide went into Monday down 19.05. Dak Prescott scored 31.4 in Cowboys–Eagles. Saquon Barkley scored 15.1 in the same game for the other side. Net gain: 16.3. Needed: 19.05. Pain.

The bench will get blamed, and the best lineup (142.1) would have won, but go look at the projections before you yell. Juwan Johnson (1.7, projected 10.3) followed last week's 0.0 with another near-zero at tight end, while Marvin Mims Jr. (7.6) and Tank Dell (5.5) sat on projections of 4.8 and 1.9. Nobody starts those guys. The real crime was Nico Collins: 2.6 points on a 17.1 projection, the worst dud of the week. Aaron Jones Sr. added 3.6 on a 12.8 projection and is now listed questionable. The two $6 waiver adds, Brandin Cooks and Roschon Johnson, combined for 3.6 on the bench. Geno-Cide falls from fifth to seventh and from 63% to 41% to make the playoffs.

ChrisUMD23 benched Michael Penix Jr. (28.55) for Goff (27.05), which looks bad until you see Goff was projected 26.7 and Penix 19.7. Correct call, cost 1.5 points, won anyway. Burden has 43.2 points in two games since coming over from Cheesehead10, and Chris has won two straight to get to 3-4. One small problem: Murrdawgs own ChrisUMD23's 2027 first, so the buyer is now playing for pride and somebody else's draft slot.
games.v: Geno-Cide Smith is 3-4 and has lost by a combined 6.6 points the last two weeks. Somebody check on Willy.

games.h: Murrdawgs Finally Hold a Monday Lead (They Had Nobody Playing)
t: Stop the presses: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor took a lead into Monday night and won. After blowing Monday leads in Week 5 and Week 6, the Massage Parlor went into Cowboys–Eagles up 30.3 with nobody left to play, which is one way to make sure your guys can't choke. degr needed 30.3 from Dallas Goedert. Goedert got 9.8.

Getting there was a 297-point slugfest. degr led 22.5 after Rhamondre Stevenson's Thursday night, Murrdawgs answered with 108.5 in the early window behind Joe Burrow (39.8, the top score of the week) and Tony Pollard (38.5 out of the flex on a 14.8 projection), and degr took it back by 3.0 after the late games with Ashton Jeanty (21.6) and Josh Jacobs (20.1). Then Jaxon Smith-Njigba went for 33.3 on Sunday night and that was it.

The Murrdawgs lineup was still a crime scene. Garrett Wilson (4.6), Derrick Henry (5.9), Isaiah Likely (3.2) and Jaylin Noel (1.7 in his Murrdawgs debut, now listed questionable) all missed their projections by 7.1 to 12.2 points, and 37.6 points sat on the bench, led by Cam Skattebo's 21.1. Skattebo was projected for 7.0, so that one is a shrug. Also: Murrdawgs dropped Sam Darnold this week, and he scored 18.55 on CeeDeez Nutz's bench. The win moves Murrdawgs to second, with bye odds up from 30% to 42%.

degr has lost four straight and sits 11th at 2-5. The best lineup (178.3) wins by 19.4, but most of what sat on the bench was projected to sit: KC Concepcion Jr. (25.2 on a 9.7 projection) and Makai Lemon (19.7 on 8.9). Brock Purdy (16.9) over Jordan Love (23.7) was a coin flip on projections. Jalen Coker was the killer, 1.9 on a 15.7 projection and now questionable. Then after the week degr traded Ollie Gordon II, who just scored 19.3, to Cheesehead10 for a 2027 second. degr's 2027 first belongs to Matty Ice, so every degr loss is a Matty Ice win.
games.v: Murrdawgs beat the Monday curse the way you beat a slot machine: by walking away from it.

games.h: PhilthyPhil Picks the Wrong Quarterback for the Second Straight Week
t: Doc, we need to talk about your quarterbacks. Last week PhilthyPhil benched C.J. Stroud and Stroud scored 34.1. This week Phil started Stroud (22.05) and benched Caleb Williams, who scored 31.2. This week Sleeper had them 0.2 points apart, so call it a curse more than malpractice. Throw in Caleb Douglas (21.0 on the bench, projected 7.7) and Christian Kirk, a $0 waiver pickup who went straight into the lineup and scored a perfectly priced 0.0.

Bijan al Gaib didn't need the help. Geno Smith scored 32.35 on a 20.6 projection, and yes, the team in this league named Geno-Cide Smith does not have Geno Smith. Amon-Ra St. Brown (26.2, now questionable with an ankle) keeps paying off the closed for business trade, Emanuel Wilson went for 20.5 on Sunday night on a 10.1 projection, and Javonte Williams (23.5) and George Pickens (15.7) closed it out on Monday. Mason Taylor scored 25.2 on the Bijan bench on a 4.4 projection, which nobody could have seen coming.

This was close for exactly one window. Phil led by 0.8 after the early games, Bijan led by 2.9 after the late games, and then it got ugly: 23.4 after Sunday night, 51.6 after Monday. Even Phil's best lineup (147.8) loses by 18.45, so the quarterback thing was a side dish. The new guys from Cheesehead10, Ryan Flournoy and Jordan Mason, debuted with 11.0 and 6.8.

Phil drops to third at 5-2 and the bye odds fall from 58% to 38%. Bijan al Gaib, the team that traded away every first from 2027 through 2029, climbs to fourth at 4-3 with playoff odds up from 87% to 96% and title odds up from 20% to 26%. Fun fact for Matty Ice: both 2027 firsts in this game belong to Matty.
games.v: PhilthyPhil has two starting quarterbacks and has started the wrong one twice in a row. That's actually kind of hard.

games.h: Cheesehead10 Starts Kirk Cousins, Wins, Cuts Kirk Cousins
t: The most valuable roster in the league is supposedly rebuilding, and it just beat the top-rated contender lineup in the league 126.35 to 103.35. Cheesehead10 led after every window. Kirk Cousins scored 27.35 at quarterback and then got released, which is the fantasy equivalent of thanking someone for dinner and blocking their number.

The rest of the Cheesehead10 win came from guys nobody projected: Omar Cooper Jr. (24.5 on a 9.4 projection), Colston Loveland (19.9 on 9.8 on Thursday night), plus Drake London (19.6, now listed questionable with a head injury). Zonovan Knight came off waivers for $0 and gave them 9.3. Seven first-round picks, two straight wins, and the playoff odds just went from 10% to 25%. The tank has a turbo button.

PerryCock, buddy. Bryce Young started and scored 9.05 on a 23.4 projection while Bo Nix sat on the bench and scored 30.5 on a 25.2 projection. Nix was projected higher. That one's a real blunder, and the best lineup (136.7) wins by 10.35. Kenneth Walker III (9.7 on 19.4) and Justin Jefferson (8.4 on 16.9) didn't help. PerryCock is third in points for and 2-5, playoff odds down from 86% to 72%, bye odds from 16% to 4%, title odds from 22% to 17%. And Matty Ice, who owns PerryCock's 2027 first, would like to thank everyone involved.
games.v: Cheesehead10 used Kirk Cousins like a rental car and returned him with a full tank.

games.h: Bad Bunny's Bush Wins Five Straight Against a Team With Nobody at Tight End
t: closed for business took the name literally this week. The tight end slot was empty. Eight starters, one blank, 88.1 points. To be fair, the best lineup was 95.8, so filling the hole wouldn't have saved anybody against 152.45.

Bad Bunny's Bush led after every window and never sweated it. Tee Higgins went for 28.8 on a 15.0 projection, Matthew Stafford had 25.45 with Josh Allen and the Bills on bye, and Puka Nacua added 21.8. Sam LaPorta's 2.8 on a 13.5 projection and Braelon Allen's 21.4 on the bench were the only blemishes. Five straight wins, 6-1, bye odds up from 78% to 85%, and second in the $400 points race, 65.85 behind Murrdawgs.

For closed for business, Jameson Williams scored 26.1 of the 88.1 and the $11 waiver pickup Jordan Watkins scored 8.6 on the bench. They're 4-3 and in sixth, which sounds great until you see they're tenth in points for and the sim gives them a 4% playoff shot. Their 2027 first belongs to Cheesehead10, so there's no tank to fall back on either. NotGomes is just out here running a 4-3 business with no inventory.
games.v: Closed for business, and closed at tight end too. At least the sign is honest.

games.h: Matty Ice Scores 53.8 and Now Owns the Three Worst Games of the Season
t: The three lowest scores of the 2026 season: 49.25, 53.8 and 58.0. All Matty Ice. The commissioner of this league fielded a quarterback (Fernando Mendoza), two running backs (Adam Randall and Raheim Sanders, both now on IR) and a receiver (Zavion Thomas) who scored a combined 0.0. Malik Nabers (20.1), Eli Raridon (14.6 on a 5.6 projection) and Brock Bowers (13.3) did all the work. There was no bench. Zero points left on it for the fourth straight week, because you can't leave points on a bench you don't have.

CeeDeez Nutz had this one locked up Thursday night when Drake Maye dropped 36.65 in Patriots–Bears. Quinshon Judkins scored 23.4 on an 11.2 projection, and CeeDee Lamb, last seen winning the Name Check award with 2.9 in Week 5, scored 24.4 on Monday night. CeeDeez also has a quarterback room of Sam Darnold (18.55, the guy Murrdawgs just dropped), Kyler Murray (17.4) and Cam Ward (7.55) on the bench in a one-quarterback league. And yes, three tight ends started again; Tyler Higbee's 3.4 cost 5.3 points against the best lineup. The 71.95-point margin was the biggest of the week.

CeeDeez is 4-3, up to fifth, playoff odds up from 33% to 45%. Matty is 1-6, three games back, 0% everything. But the 1.01 is locked: non-playoff teams pick by reverse Maximum Points For, and Matty's Max PF of 642.3 is 234.7 below anyone else. Every perfectly efficient 53.8 is another brick in the draft room.
games.v: CeeDeez won the game by 71.95. Matty's draft pick won by more.

awards.p: Top score of the week, 14.0 over projection, and the reason Murrdawgs were up big enough to survive a Monday.
Second straight week Phil's bench quarterback wins this award. Last week it was C.J. Stroud's 34.1.
The closest game of the season, one week after losing the second-closest by 3.85. Dak's 31.4 on Monday wasn't enough.
Projected for 14.8 and beat it by 23.7, the biggest surprise of the week, out of a flex spot.
Zero points left on the bench for the fourth straight week, with four starters at 0.0. Efficiency is easy when there's no bench.
Started at quarterback, scored 27.35 in a win, then got cut.

awards.p: Picked up for $0 and put straight into the lineup. Scored exactly what he cost.
Top team score of the week, led by Geno Smith's 32.35, in a 51.6-point win over the second-place team.
Projected for 17.1, scored 2.6, and his team lost by 2.75.
