7.note: Monday night's Cowboys–Eagles decided the closest game of the season, Sunday night's Chiefs–Seahawks put Murrdawgs ahead for good, and Thursday's Patriots–Bears gave CeeDeez Nutz and ChrisUMD23 big early leads.

8.dek: Bad Bunny's Bush hangs a season-high 201.35 on Geno-Cide Smith, Joe Burrow drops 54.1, and CeeDeez Nutz loses the closest game of the year by 1.3 with 84.7 points of quarterback on the bench. Matty Ice scores 40.7, then goes shopping.

stories.h: CeeDeez Nutz loses the closest game of the season with 84.7 points of quarterback on the bench
stories.body: PerryCock 123.35, CeeDeez Nutz 122.05. That 1.3 is the new closest game of 2026, and for once Geno-Cide Smith wasn't involved. Cam Ward (35.3), Kyler Murray (26.0) and Sam Darnold (23.4) combined for 84.7 on the CeeDeez bench, the exact number ChrisUMD23's entire team scored this week. Drake Maye was still the right start at 28.45, so save the outrage for the running backs: Jeremiyah Love scored 2.3 with no Sleeper projection and Elijah Mitchell, a $0 pickup, had 7.7 on the bench. That swap wins it. PerryCock jumps from tenth to eighth, playoff odds up from 74% to 87%, and at 3-5 now has the second-best title odds in the league at 20%. The simulation has seen the roster and does not care about your record.

stories.h: closed for business changes its name, then sells everything in sight
stories.body: The team formerly known as closed for business is now Open for Business, and NotGomes meant it. On Monday, Michael Wilson and a 2029 third went to PerryCock for three second-round picks. A little over two hours later Tetairoa McMillan and Jaxson Dart went to Matty Ice for the 2027 firsts from degr and Bijan al Gaib, plus Matty's own 2027 second and 2028 third. NotGomes went from one first-round pick to three, and sold Wilson right after a 28.8. The catch: Lamar Jackson is now the only quarterback on the roster and is listed out with a thumb, and Aaron Rodgers got cut last Thursday. The team is 4-4 with a 1% playoff shot, so maybe the QB room can wait. Next week: PerryCock, starring Michael Wilson, now listed questionable with ribs.

stories.h: Murrdawgs score 188.2 and the $400 race got tighter
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor put up 188.2 behind a 54.1 from Joe Burrow, and the lead in the points race went down. Bad Bunny's Bush dropped a season-high 201.35 and now sits 52.7 back, 1,290.1 to 1,237.4, after trailing by 65.85 a week ago. PhilthyPhil is 139.35 back and PerryCock fell to 153.6 back. This is a two-team race with six regular-season weeks of arguing left. Bad Bunny's has won six straight and leads the title odds at 26%. Murrdawgs sit at 19%. Rulebook reminder: a points leader who doesn't reach the championship game picks 1.10, so whoever takes the $400 still has to show up in December.

stories.h: The all-play table says this league is a lie
stories.body: Cheesehead10 is 4-4 with a 29-59 all-play record. Open for Business is 4-4 at 28-60. degr is 2-6 at 50-38, and PerryCock is 3-5 at 56-32. Those two 4-4 teams are ninth and tenth in points for. This week was the whole thing in miniature: Open for Business scored 98.1 and lost by 90.1, while Bijan al Gaib (96.7) and Cheesehead10 (94.55) both scored less and won. Geno-Cide Smith has now given up the most points in the league (1,161.15), with degr right behind at 1,151.8. The sim only believes some of it: PerryCock 87%, Cheesehead10 47%, degr 12%, Open for Business 1%. NotGomes, you're a game ahead of PerryCock in the standings and 86 points behind in the sim.

stories.h: The race for 1.01 is over, so the fight is for 1.02
stories.body: Matty Ice is the 1.01 in every simulation: a 683.0 Maximum Points For sits 329.8 below the next-lowest team, and non-playoff teams draft by reverse Max PF. Below that, look who gets paid. Open for Business projects at an average slot of 2.05, and that pick belongs to Cheesehead10. ChrisUMD23 projects at 3.41, and that pick belongs to Murrdawgs. So the two best firsts outside Matty's are owned by a 4-4 rebuild and a 6-2 contender. ChrisUMD23's 152.9 best lineup this week was the highest of any losing team, and every point of it nudges Murrdawgs' pick later. Meanwhile degr's first, which Matty just sold, projects at only 5.86 despite the 2-6 record, since degr's 1,208.6 Max PF is fifth in the league. That's Max PF for you: degr can lose every week from here and still pick in the middle.

stories.h: Somebody started a Saint on bye
stories.body: The league left 251.6 points on its benches, and two results flipped on them. CeeDeez Nutz is the one everybody will talk about, and ChrisUMD23 is the one everybody should. Alvin Kamara plays for New Orleans, New Orleans had the week off, and Kamara started anyway for a clean 0.0 in a 9.85-point loss with Kenny Gainwell (16.0) on the bench. ChrisUMD23 left 68.2 points on the pine, most in the league. Elsewhere, PhilthyPhil's quarterback curse got a week off too, since C.J. Stroud's Texans were on bye and the decision made itself. Phil promptly found a new coin to lose: Dalton Kincaid (18.6, projected 10.5) over Harold Fannin Jr. (25.4, projected 10.6). Phil cannot catch a break on a coin flip.

games.h: Four Quarterbacks, One Roster, 1.3 Points Short
t: Geno-Cide Smith has finally been relieved of duty. The closest game of the 2026 season now belongs to CeeDeez Nutz, who lost 123.35 to 122.05 while Cam Ward (35.3), Kyler Murray (26.0) and Sam Darnold (23.4) sat on the bench and watched. That's 84.7 points of benched quarterback in a one-quarterback league. It is also, to the decimal, what ChrisUMD23's entire team scored this week. DylanDaKing has built the world's most expensive bullpen and it does not pitch.

Now the fair part, because the mob will get this wrong. Drake Maye scored 28.45 on a 26.1 projection and Ward was projected for 15.4. Starting Maye was correct. The actual problem was at running back, where Jeremiyah Love started with no Sleeper projection, scored 2.3 and is now listed out with an ankle, while Elijah Mitchell, a $0 waiver pickup from last week, scored 7.7 on the bench. That swap wins the game. So does Mark Andrews (4.4) over Tyler Higbee (2.4), although Higbee was projected higher and that one is a shrug. CeeDee Lamb's 12.8 on a 22.1 projection didn't help either.

PerryCock has its own quarterback saga. Bryce Young started again and scored 14.45 on a 22.5 projection while Bo Nix put up 25.5 on the bench. Last week that was a real blunder because Nix was projected higher. This week Sleeper had Young up 4.2, so austinp247 gets a pass and a stern look. Ja'Marr Chase saved everyone with 33.1 on a 19.8 projection, then on Monday PerryCock went out and bought Michael Wilson anyway.

The timeline was a heart attack with a very quiet ending. CeeDeez led by 27.75 after Thursday behind Chuba Hubbard (24.9) and Tucker Kraft (17.3). PerryCock was up 35.05 after the early games. Maye and DeMario Douglas cut it to 11.7, and Antonio Williams' 10.4 on Sunday night cut it to 1.3. Then both teams ran out of players, so Monday night was two managers staring at a final score. PerryCock climbs from tenth to eighth, playoff odds up from 74% to 87%. CeeDeez stays fifth at 4-4, odds down from 39% to 32%.
games.v: Four quarterbacks on the roster, one start allowed, and the season's closest game came down to a running back scoring 2.3. Art.

games.h: Geno-Cide Smith Fixes the Close-Game Problem
t: Last week this website told Willy to start beating people by 40 just to be safe, after back-to-back losses by 3.85 and 2.75. Willy took the note, turned it upside down, and lost by 125.2. That's the biggest blowout of the season, handed out by the highest score of the season, 201.35. Nobody can say Geno-Cide lost a close one this time.

Bad Bunny's Bush had five guys at 25 or more. Tee Higgins went for 39.5 on a 16.0 projection, Josh Allen had 33.45, D'Andre Swift dropped 27.9 on Monday night just to run up the score, Braelon Allen got promoted from last week's bench to 25.3, and Puka Nacua had exactly 25.0. Jonathan Taylor (6.7 on a 16.4 projection) and Sam LaPorta (6.5) were the only guys who didn't get the memo, and they still left just 4.7 on the bench. Six straight wins, 7-1, bye odds up from 79% to 87%.

Over on the crime scene: Zay Flowers scored 0.0 on an 18.5 projection, DK Metcalf had 1.4 on 11.1, and Kyren Williams managed 12.9 on 20.1. Patrick Mahomes scored 36.65 on the bench while Dak Prescott scored 23.75, and before anyone starts yelling, Dak was projected 30.1 and Mahomes 22.7. Right call. It also wouldn't have mattered, since the best lineup was 93.95 and that loses by 107.4.

Geno-Cide drops from seventh to ninth, the playoff odds crash from 41% to 24%, and the team now leads the league in points allowed at 1,161.15. Next up is Matty Ice, the one matchup on the schedule with no margin for embarrassment.
games.v: Lost by 2.75 last week, lost by 125.2 this week. Somebody check on Willy again, and bring a bigger search party.

games.h: Burrow 54.1, Lamar 0.0, Please Exit Through the Gift Shop
t: Joe Burrow scored 54.1 points. Lamar Jackson scored 0.0 points. That's the game. You can go home. If you stay, Tony Pollard scored 30.7 on a 14.3 projection in the same Bengals-Titans shootout, and the Burrow-Pollard parlay alone (84.8) beats ChrisUMD23's whole team by a tenth of a point.

Open for Business actually led for a little while, by 11.8, because Tetairoa McMillan played Thursday and Murrdawgs hadn't started yet. Then the early window hit and it was 81.9 the other way. Lamar's 0.0 was the biggest miss against projection in the entire league, 25.4 points' worth, and Lamar is now listed out with a thumb. No lineup call to second-guess there: the other quarterback on the roster, Jaxson Dart, had the week off with the Giants, and Aaron Rodgers got cut on Thursday. Michael Wilson (28.8) and Jonah Coleman (20.4) tried, and then NotGomes traded Wilson and McMillan on Monday anyway, because this team's name is apparently a promise.

Murrdawgs left 1.3 points on the bench. That's almost rude. Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 25.8 on Monday night, and the Monday curse stays dead when you're up 82.9 going in. Pat Freiermuth, a $1 waiver claim, gave them 11.6 at tight end and was cut before Tuesday, which earns a spot in the Kirk Cousins wing of the Thanks for the Memories museum. The funniest part: 188.2 points moved the bye odds from 61% to 61%. Murrdawgs are 6-2 and still second, because Bad Bunny's Bush refuses to lose.

Open for Business falls to seventh at 4-4 with a 1% playoff shot. A 101.6 best lineup is good news for exactly one person, and it's Wonderman, because Cheesehead10 owns this team's 2027 first and non-playoff slots run on Max PF.
games.v: Open for Business opened Thursday night, closed by Sunday afternoon, and held a liquidation sale before Monday kickoff.

games.h: degr Wins Thursday by 64.8, Forgets About Sunday
t: For one glorious long weekend, degr had the best team in fantasy football. Jordan Love went for 30.4 on Thursday night, Josh Jacobs had 23.2, Matthew Golden had 20.9, and degr woke up Friday leading 84.1 to 19.3. Love, you'll remember, came over from Matty Ice in Week 5, and for three days that trade looked like grand larceny.

Then Sunday at 1:00 happened. PhilthyPhil scored 112.0 in the early window. degr scored 17.0. That's a 95-point swing, from down 64.8 to up 30.2, in about three hours. Bhayshul Tuten went for 31.9 on a 15.3 projection, Jahmyr Gibbs had 26.8, Bucky Irving had 23.0 and Dalton Kincaid added 18.6. degr's entire early window was Ashton Jeanty (10.3 on a 15.9 projection) and KC Concepcion Jr. (6.7).

Phil's quarterback controversy took the week off because C.J. Stroud's Texans did. Caleb Williams started by default and scored 18.45. Naturally Phil found something else to agonize over: Harold Fannin Jr. scored 25.4 on the bench on a 10.6 projection, while Kincaid started on 10.5. That is three straight weeks Phil has picked wrong between two guys, and it is getting personal. The win puts Phil at 6-2 and playoff odds at 100%.

degr has now lost five straight at 2-6, and the playoff odds slid from 18% to 12%. The best lineup (151.7) still loses by 16.35, so no one gets to blame the $0 pickup Gunnar Helm's 14.6 on the bench. And with a 50-38 all-play record, this might be the most unlucky bad team in America. degr's 2027 first left Matty Ice for Open for Business on Monday, so NotGomes gets to enjoy the streak now. And the day after Jacobs' 23.2, degr sent Jacobs and its 2027 second to Bad Bunny's Bush for A.J. Brown, who scored 0.0 on the degr bench. First place got richer while degr was still spending Thursday's lead.
games.v: degr won Thursday by 64.8. Unfortunately the league insists on playing the other days too.

games.h: ChrisUMD23 Starts a Saint on the Saints' Bye
t: Alvin Kamara plays for the New Orleans Saints. The New Orleans Saints did not play in Week 8. Alvin Kamara started for ChrisUMD23 and scored 0.0. Sleeper had no projection at all, because Sleeper owns a calendar. Kenny Gainwell was sitting right there with a 7.2 projection and scored 16.0. Final margin: 9.85. Do the math, Chris. Actually, please don't, it'll only hurt.

The rest of the bench we'll forgive. Adonai Mitchell (29.2 on a 5.7 projection) and Emmett Johnson (27.3 on 4.4) were two of the best bench games of the week and nobody on earth was starting them. But the total damage was 68.2 points left on the bench, most in the league, and a 152.9 best lineup, which also helps push ChrisUMD23's first later for Murrdawgs, who own it. Tre Tucker went from 23.3 last week to 0.0. Michael Penix Jr. scored -0.65 on the bench, so at least Jared Goff (12.8) over Penix was correct.

Cheesehead10 was barely less silly. Tyler Allgeier scored 38.1 on the bench, the biggest bench game in the league, on an 8.3 projection, so no jail time. Drake London scored 1.8 on a 16.5 projection and is still listed questionable with a head injury, and Omar Cooper Jr. went from last week's 24.5 to 0.0. They won with 94.55, the lowest winning score of the week, because Jayden Daniels (19.15) and Rachaad White (14.0) outscored Saquon Barkley's 12.4 on Sunday night to flip a 3.8-point deficit into a 16.95-point lead. Luther Burden's 18.6 on Monday only got it back to 9.85.

Three straight wins for the league's most valuable roster. Cheesehead10 jumps from eighth to sixth with playoff odds up from 32% to 47%, and the tier label still says rebuild. Wonderman, you hold seven firsts and a playoff spot. Pick a lane, or keep driving on both shoulders. ChrisUMD23 is 3-5 and tenth, down to 1%.
games.v: Kamara had the week off. So did whoever was checking the ChrisUMD23 lineup.

games.h: Matty Ice Scores 40.7, Then Goes Shopping
t: The commissioner has done it again. The four lowest scores of the 2026 season are now 40.7, 49.25, 53.8 and 58.0, and every one of them belongs to Matty Ice. Brock Bowers scored 28.2 on a 17.2 projection, which is 69% of the team's points. The other eight starters combined for 12.5. Fernando Mendoza, Adam Randall, Pat Bryant and Jack Bech all posted 0.0, Randall and Bryant are now listed on IR, and Malik Nabers' Giants were on bye. Zero points on the bench for the fifth straight week. It's the most efficient disaster in sports.

So what do you do after the worst score of the season? You buy. On Monday, Matty Ice sent the 2027 firsts from degr and Bijan al Gaib, plus Matty's own 2027 second and 2028 third, to Open for Business for Tetairoa McMillan and Jaxson Dart. Then Matty cut J.J. McCarthy, last week's $10 waiver claim, after zero starts. The trade model has Open for Business winning that deal by 1,154 points of value, 12.9% of the deal. A 1-7 team is now down to seven first-round picks, which is a sentence that only makes sense in this league.

Bijan al Gaib deserves a word, mostly a concerned one. Three of the week's six biggest duds were on this roster: Bijan Robinson (7.6 on 21.9), Javonte Williams (6.7 on 19.8) and Parker Washington (3.6 on 14.9). The team named after Bijan got 7.6 from Bijan. They scored 96.7, eighth-most of the week, and won by 56 because of who was across the field. Trevor Lawrence's 27.5 did the heavy lifting, and the team finished 5-3 with bye odds actually falling, from 21% to 13%, as the teams above them scored like maniacs.

Matty is 1-7 and three games back, with 0% everything. The 1.01 is safe: a 683.0 Max PF is 329.8 below the next-lowest team in the league. Every first-round pick Matty sold is one less reason to watch anybody else's games, but don't worry, the Geno-Cide Smith matchup next week should be appointment television for all the wrong reasons.
games.v: Matty Ice scored 40.7, and the 1.01 scored another touchdown.

awards.p: Top score of the week by 14.6 points and 25.4 over projection. Second straight week winning this award.
Ward, Murray and Darnold combined for 84.7 on the bench in a one-quarterback league, in a game lost by 1.3.
Started a Saint with the Saints on bye and lost by 9.85. Kenny Gainwell scored 16.0 on the bench.
The lowest score of the season, with zero left on the bench for the fifth straight week. Peak efficiency, on the worst possible scale.
Projected for 25.4, the biggest miss in the league, and now listed out with a thumb.
The highest score of 2026 and the biggest margin of 2026, 125.2, in the same game. Six straight wins.
The biggest bench score of the week, on an 8.3 projection, in a game Cheesehead10 won anyway.
Claimed for $1, started at tight end, scored 11.6, and got cut before Tuesday. That's 11.6 points per dollar.

awards.a: You Get What You Pay For
awards.p: The week's biggest waiver bid at $21 bought 1.9 points on the bench, right on the 1.8 projection.
Changed the team name, then sold McMillan, Dart and Wilson on Monday and went from one first-round pick to three.

8.note: Titans-Bengals in the early window set up the week's biggest scores, Panthers-Packers on Thursday gave degr a 64.8-point lead that Sunday erased, Eagles-Commanders on Sunday night put Cheesehead10 ahead for good and cut PerryCock-CeeDeez Nutz to 1.3, and Monday's Bears-Seahawks changed no results.

9.dek: CeeDeez Nutz erase a 16.75-point Thursday hole and knock Murrdawgs out of the bye seat, PerryCock hangs 190.15 on the team that sold it Michael Wilson, and PhilthyPhil benches the wrong quarterback for the third straight week. This time the wrong one scored 51.2.

stories.h: CeeDeez Nutz come back on Murrdawgs and blow up the bye race
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor took a 16.75-point lead out of Thursday night and never saw it again. CeeDee Lamb dropped 35.5, Drake Maye added 27.25, DeMario Douglas turned an 8.8 projection into 17.2, and CeeDeez Nutz won 124.05 to 113.0. One week after losing the closest game of the year with 84.7 points of quarterback on the bench, DylanDaKing left a grand total of 2.1 points on the pine. Growth. The swing is real: CeeDeez go from 34% to 54% to make the playoffs, and Murrdawgs drop from second to third with their bye odds cut from 62% to 38%.

stories.h: PhilthyPhil has now lost the quarterback coin flip three weeks running
stories.body: Week 6: Caleb Williams starts, C.J. Stroud scores 34.1 on the bench. Week 7: Stroud starts, Williams scores 31.2 on the bench. Week 9: Williams starts (19.55, projected 23.8) and Stroud scores 51.2 on the bench, the highest score by any player in the league this week. Sleeper had Williams up by 2.6, so the call was defensible, and the call was also wrong, again. Phil left 44.15 points on the bench, most in the league, won by 59.25 anyway, and moved into second at 7-2 with bye odds up from 44% to 63%. Imagine being this good and this cursed at the same time.

stories.h: PerryCock scores 190.15 and crashes the $400 points race
stories.body: A week ago this was a two-team race. Then PerryCock put up 190.15, the fourth-highest score of the season, and cut its deficit from 153.6 to 76.45. Murrdawgs still lead with 1,403.1, Bad Bunny's Bush is 56.1 back at 1,347.0, PerryCock sits third at 1,326.65 and PhilthyPhil is 107.8 back. Murrdawgs scored 113.0 in a loss and somehow padded the lead over Bad Bunny's. The $400 goes to the regular-season points leader, so five weeks of every manager in the top four refreshing the scoreboard to see who else is losing starts now.

stories.h: Four teams are 4-5 and they have nothing in common
stories.body: PerryCock, Geno-Cide Smith, Cheesehead10 and Open for Business are all 4-5. PerryCock has a 67-32 all-play record and an 84% playoff shot. Geno-Cide Smith is 49-50 and sits at 18%. Cheesehead10 is 31-68 and fell from sixth to eighth, playoff odds down from 54% to 33%. Open for Business is 32-67 and is at 1%. Same record, four completely different seasons. PerryCock holds the sixth and last playoff spot after allowing 1,241.55 points, second-most in the league, which is the fantasy version of getting mugged every week and still making rent.

stories.h: The trade box score: revenge for PerryCock, a doughnut for Bad Bunny's
stories.body: Michael Wilson, sold by Open for Business to PerryCock in Week 8, played his old team and scored 12.0 in a 96.55-point beating. He is now listed out with a neck injury. Josh Jacobs, the return on the A.J. Brown deal, scored 0.5 on a 15.0 projection for Bad Bunny's Bush and has since been ruled out with a finger injury. Tyler Allgeier, who scored 38.1 on Cheesehead10's bench last week, debuted for Murrdawgs with 6.6 in a loss. And over on degr's bench, Jordan Love, the quarterback degr pried from Matty Ice in Week 5, put up 47.9. Matty's new guy Tetairoa McMillan did score 15.6, so Matt has that.

stories.h: The race for 1.02 got tighter, and Cheesehead10 and Murrdawgs are the ones sweating
stories.body: Matty Ice is the 1.01 in every simulation with a 776.2 Maximum Points For, 344.0 below anyone else. Non-playoff teams draft by reverse Max PF, so the real fight is one spot down. Open for Business sits at 1,120.2 and ChrisUMD23 at 1,132.99, a gap of 12.79 that was 17.09 a week ago. Open for Business's first belongs to Cheesehead10 and projects at an average slot of 2.14. ChrisUMD23's belongs to Murrdawgs and projects at 3.2. Neither NotGomes nor ChrisUMD23 gains anything by losing, so this is two other managers rooting for bad lineups they do not control.

games.h: CeeDeez Nutz Spot Murrdawgs 16.75 on Thursday, Then Take the Bye Seat Hostage
t: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor went to bed Thursday up 16.75 thanks to Chris Rodriguez Jr. (11.2) and Derrick Henry in Jacksonville's rout of Baltimore. CeeDeez Nutz had nobody in that game and spent the next 60 hours making it irrelevant. By the end of the early Sunday games CeeDeez led by 2.8, by the end of the late games they led by 20.65, and Murrdawgs never got closer than 11.05.

CeeDee Lamb did the heavy lifting with 35.5 on a 21.4 projection. Drake Maye added 27.25 and DeMario Douglas went for 17.2 on an 8.8 projection, which is the kind of flex call that looks genius on Tuesday. Tucker Kraft (1.9 on an 11.3 projection) tried to give it back and nobody let him. The best part: one week after losing by 1.3 with 84.7 points of quarterback on the bench, CeeDeez left just 2.1 points on the pine. Somebody read the recap.

Murrdawgs got 38.25 from Joe Burrow and almost nothing from the receivers: Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 12.1 on a 24.0 projection and George Kittle managed 9.8. New guy Tyler Allgeier debuted with 6.6 on a 13.6 projection, one week after scoring 38.1 on Cheesehead10's bench. Blake Corum (7.2 projected) starting over Isaiah Likely (11.1) is the call you can yell about, though Corum scored 11.8 and Likely's 16.3 alone doesn't close an 11.05-point gap. The full best lineup (128.95) would have, so this one counts as left on the table.

The fallout is big. CeeDeez jump from 34% to 54% to make the playoffs and sit fifth. Murrdawgs slide from second to third, their bye odds crash from 62% to 38%, and the only consolation is a 56.1-point lead in the $400 race.
games.v: Murrdawgs led for one night. CeeDeez led for the other three days, which in this sport is called winning.

games.h: Bijan al Gaib Mugs the First-Place Team Before It Even Suits Up
t: Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington combined for 32.1 on Thursday night, and Bad Bunny's Bush had zero players in the game. That was the lead after one window, it was 47.4 after the early Sunday slate, and the first-place team spent the rest of the weekend chasing a car that had already left the lot. Final: 141.7 to 109.6.

Bijan al Gaib got 28.7 from Bijan Robinson, 24.4 from Javonte Williams and 15.5 from Courtland Sutton on a 7.3 projection. The bench held 3.9 points. That is a manager who set a lineup and then went outside.

Bad Bunny's Bush had Puka Nacua (37.0) and Tee Higgins (20.2) and basically nothing at running back. D'Andre Swift scored 3.1 on a 19.2 projection on Sunday night, and Josh Jacobs, the prize of the A.J. Brown trade, scored 0.5 on a 15.0 projection and has since been ruled out with a finger injury. Jordan Watkins, picked up for $0 this week, scored 18.6 on the bench on a 7.2 projection, which is a fair call that hurt. Even the perfect lineup (139.0) loses this one. Puka is now listed questionable with a knee, so circle that.
Bad Bunny's stays in first at 7-2 on the tiebreaker with PhilthyPhil, but its bye odds dropped from 86% to 76%. Bijan al Gaib has won three straight and its bye odds jumped from 6% to 19%.
games.v: Bad Bunny's Bush lost the game on Thursday and spent four days filing the paperwork.

games.h: Michael Wilson Visits His Old Team and PerryCock Burns the Store Down
t: Last week NotGomes sold Michael Wilson to PerryCock for three seconds. This week Wilson lined up against Open for Business and scored 12.0, and he was only the eighth-best starter on his own team. PerryCock won 190.15 to 93.6, the biggest margin of the week at 96.55, and led by 100.75 before the late games even kicked off.

Kenneth Walker III scored 38.3 on a 21.7 projection. Ja'Marr Chase added 33.5, Christian McCaffrey 22.7, Bo Nix 22.05, and James Cook III tacked on 18.7 on Monday night just to be rude. Justin Jefferson's 8.8 on an 18.3 projection was the only bad thing that happened, and Bryce Young sat on the bench with 29.1 after Sleeper projected him two points higher than Nix. With a lineup this loaded nobody noticed.

Open for Business started Kirk Cousins (16.8), yes, the same Kirk Cousins Cheesehead10 rented and cut in Week 7. Ja'Kobi Lane gave them a 0.0 and Kaleb Johnson scored 12.8 on the bench on a 0.6 projection, a fair benching. Wilson is now listed out with a neck injury, so enjoy the revenge game, NotGomes, you may not see him for a bit.

PerryCock is 4-5, has won two straight and climbs from eighth to sixth, the last playoff spot. Open for Business falls to ninth with a 1% playoff shot, and since its first belongs to Cheesehead10, every loss is free entertainment for nobody on that roster.
games.v: Open for Business sold Michael Wilson for three seconds and got 96.55 points of buyer's remorse as a receipt.

games.h: PhilthyPhil Benches 51.2 Points of Quarterback and Wins by 59 Anyway
t: C.J. Stroud scored 51.2 points this week. More than any player in the league. He did it on PhilthyPhil's bench, because Phil started Caleb Williams (19.55) for the third straight week of picking the wrong one. Sleeper had Williams projected 2.6 points higher, so the logic holds up. The results have stopped caring about the logic.

It didn't matter, because Christian Watson went for 32.1 on a 15.9 projection and Bucky Irving added 28.5 on Sunday night. PhilthyPhil left 44.15 on the bench, the most in the league, and still beat Cheesehead10 144.55 to 85.3. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 13.4 on a 25.7 projection and it was still a blowout.

Cheesehead10 had a rough one. Drake London scored 11.8 on an 18.4 projection, Jameson Williams scored 5.0 on 13.3, and Jordan Addison scored 4.8 on Monday night. Audric Estime, a $0 pickup this week, scored 14.7 on the bench while Ollie Gordon II scored 7.4 at running back, though Sleeper had Gordon projected 6.4 higher, so that's a fair call that missed. Even the best lineup (112.4) loses by 32.

PhilthyPhil moves to 7-2 and second, bye odds up from 44% to 63%. Cheesehead10 drops from sixth to eighth and its playoff odds fall from 54% to 33%. With seven firsts on the roster, Wonderman might be fine with that.
games.v: PhilthyPhil has three quarterbacks' worth of regret and a 7-2 record. Life is unfair, mostly to Cheesehead10.

games.h: Matty Ice Starts a Quarterback Who Scores Zero and Loses a Game He Led
t: Matty Ice led this game. Please sit with that. After the early Sunday games Matt was up 49.8 to 43.25, then Dak Prescott and the late window happened and Geno-Cide Smith won 89.55 to 82.3. For Willy, who lost the two closest games of the season back to back, a 7.25-point win is a spa day.

The quarterback slot is where this went sideways. Fernando Mendoza started with no Sleeper projection at all, and he delivered exactly that: 0.0. Dak scored 28.85 on the other side. Adam Randall also started with no projection, scored 0.0, and is now on IR. That's two dead slots in a game decided by 7.25.

And the receipt for the loss is sitting right there: Efton Chism III scored 15.9 on the bench on a 6.6 projection while Jordyn Tyson started at 4.8 projected and scored 5.0. Sleeper liked Chism more. Matt went the other way. That one swap makes it 93.2 to 89.55, a Matty Ice win. On the bright side, Brock Bowers scored 24.3 and Tetairoa McMillan put up 15.6 on a 13.8 projection.

Geno-Cide Smith left 27.2 on its own bench (Tank Dell's 22.5 on a 2.8 projection is forgivable) and moves to 4-5, level with PerryCock for the last playoff spot but sitting seventh on the outside with 18% odds. Matty Ice is 1-8 and still the 1.01 in every simulation, and after three straight weeks with the league's lowest score, finally handed that title to someone else.
games.v: Matty Ice found a way to lose with a lead and an 82.3. Progress is a staircase, Matt, and you're on the basement one.

games.h: Jared Goff Scores 7.0 and ChrisUMD23 Takes Over the Basement for a Week
t: Sleeper projected Jared Goff for 26.4. Goff scored 7.0, a 19.4-point miss and the biggest dud of the week, and ChrisUMD23 finished with 78.6, the lowest score in the league. Congrats to Chris for ending Matty Ice's three-week stranglehold on the weekly basement.

degr won this one in the late Sunday window, putting up 87.8 points while Chris added 16.0. Matthew Golden scored 34.4 on a 14.9 projection, the biggest surprise in the league, and Brock Purdy added 31.6. The final was 139.4 to 78.6, and degr did it with Jordan Love scoring 47.9 on the bench. Love was projected 22.1 and Purdy 27.8, so starting Purdy was the right call. Still, 47.9 on the pine from the guy degr got from Matty Ice in Week 5 is a lot of points to watch from the couch.

The rest of the Chris lineup is a medical chart. Jaylen Waddle scored 3.2 and is now listed out with a head injury, and Xavier Worthy scored 10.8 and is now out with a hamstring. Michael Penix Jr. scored 17.1 on the bench, but Goff was projected 5 points higher, so that's a bad beat. Even the best lineup (103.1) loses by 36.3.
degr moves to 3-6, tenth, with a 13% playoff shot. ChrisUMD23 drops to 11th at 3-6 and its first belongs to Murrdawgs, so Chris has nothing to play for except pride and a 23-76 all-play record.
games.v: degr scored 139.4 with a 47.9 on the bench. ChrisUMD23 scored 78.6 with nobody to blame but a guy projected for 26.4.

awards.p: Top starter in the league, 16.6 over his projection, and the headliner in a 190.15-point beatdown.
The highest score of any player in the league this week, and it came off the bench. Third straight week Phil started the wrong quarterback.

awards.who: degr · Jordan Love 47.9 on the bench
awards.p: The second-best bench score of the week from the quarterback degr acquired from Matty Ice in Week 5. degr won by 60.8 anyway.

The fourth-highest score of the season and the biggest margin of the week, 96.55 over Open for Business.
Projected for 14.9 and beat it by 19.5, the biggest surprise of the week.
Traded from Open for Business to PerryCock in Week 8, then scored 12.0 against them in a 96.55-point win. Now listed out with a neck injury.

awards.a: You Get What You Pay For
awards.who: Bad Bunny's Bush · Jordan Watkins 18.6 on the bench
awards.p: A $0 waiver pickup scored 18.6 on the bench in his first week while D'Andre Swift scored 3.1 in the lineup. Bad Bunny's lost by 32.1.
Fernando Mendoza and Adam Randall both started without a Sleeper projection and both scored zero in a 7.25-point loss.
Lowest score of the week, ending Matty Ice's three-week run in the basement.

9.note: Thursday's Jaguars-Ravens game gave Bijan al Gaib a 32.1-point head start, the late Sunday window swung CeeDeez Nutz over Murrdawgs and put degr up by 86.3, and Monday's Bills-Vikings game added James Cook III's 18.7 to PerryCock's pile.

10.dek: PerryCock climbs out of a 68.65-point hole on PhilthyPhil, Murrdawgs drop a season-high 220.85 on the team they sold Derrick Henry to, and four teams are now tied at 7-3. The commissioner started a running back on injured reserve. Again.

stories.h: PerryCock comes back from 68.65 down, and PhilthyPhil's bench curse switches positions
stories.body: PhilthyPhil's entire lineup played in the early Sunday window, and when it was over Phil led 151.55 to 82.9 with nothing left to do but watch. Then Christian McCaffrey dropped 48.3 in San Francisco's 46-40 win in Dallas, Ja'Marr Chase added 34.1 on Sunday night, and PerryCock won 165.3 to 151.55. Phil left 37.7 points on the bench, most in the league: Deebo Samuel Sr. (25.9) and Ryan Flournoy (19.1) sat behind Christian Watson (6.7) and Denzel Boston (2.6). Sleeper liked the starters, so it's the quarterback saga all over again in a new position group: defensible, wrong, and the best lineup wins by 23.95. PerryCock has won three straight and its playoff odds jumped from 82% to 91%. Phil is still 7-3, but the bye odds slipped from 69% to 64%.

stories.h: Four teams at 7-3, two byes, four weeks to sort it out
stories.body: Murrdawgs Massage Parlor, PhilthyPhil, Bad Bunny's Bush and Bijan al Gaib are all 7-3, and only two of them get a week off in the playoffs. Murrdawgs sit on top thanks to points, with bye odds up from 43% to 56%. Phil is at 64%. Bijan al Gaib has won four straight and went from 16% to 36%. And Bad Bunny's Bush, which won six in a row from Week 3 to Week 8, has now lost two straight and watched its bye odds crash from 68% to 38%, the biggest drop of the week. jambosti went from first to third in one Sunday. Every game from here to Week 14 is a bye elimination game for somebody.

stories.h: Murrdawgs score 220.85 and turn the $400 race into a parade
stories.body: A week ago the points race had a 56.1-point gap at the top. Then Murrdawgs hung 220.85, the highest score of the 2026 season, while Bad Bunny's Bush put up 93.6. Murrdawgs now have 1,623.95. PerryCock is second, 132.0 back. PhilthyPhil is 177.1 back and Bad Bunny's Bush fell to 183.35 back. Four regular-season weeks are left, so the math says Connorj22 can start picking out what to buy with the $400. The rulebook says one more thing, though: a points leader who doesn't reach the championship game picks 1.10. The money's nice. December still counts.

stories.h: The 5-5 club has four members and the worst one holds the last playoff seat
stories.body: PerryCock, Geno-Cide Smith, CeeDeez Nutz and Cheesehead10 are all 5-5. PerryCock is fifth with a 76-34 all-play record and a 91% playoff shot after allowing a league-high 1,393.1 points. The sixth and final spot belongs to Geno-Cide Smith, whose playoff odds are 21%, the lowest of the three bubble teams at 5-5. CeeDeez Nutz fell from fifth to seventh and dropped from 59% to 35%. Cheesehead10 is eighth at 26%, and degr is lurking at 4-6 after jumping from 16% to 26% with two straight wins. Translation: the sim thinks the last ticket goes to whoever stops tripping first.

stories.h: The trade box score: Henry gets revenge on nobody, St. Brown gets it on his old team
stories.body: Murrdawgs traded Derrick Henry to ChrisUMD23 for a 2029 first last Thursday, the schedule made them play this week, and Henry scored 19.0 on Monday night in a 97.9-point loss. Amon-Ra St. Brown, who went from Open for Business (then closed for business) to Bijan al Gaib in Week 5, scored 25.8 against his old team in the biggest blowout of the season. A.J. Brown, sent from Bad Bunny's Bush to degr in Week 6, scored 4.7 in degr's win over Bad Bunny's and has since been ruled out with a hamstring injury. And Ollie Gordon II scored 15.5 for Cheesehead10 on Sunday, then got shipped to PhilthyPhil that same afternoon for a 2027 third and a 2028 second. Cheesehead10 is 5-5 and selling. Phil is 7-3 and buying. Everybody knows exactly who they are.

stories.h: Race for 1.02: NotGomes pulls away, and Cheesehead10 is the one smiling
stories.body: Matty Ice is the 1.01 in every simulation with an 846.75 Maximum Points For, 376.9 below anyone else. Non-playoff teams draft by reverse Max PF, so the real fight is for 1.02, and it just got less close. Open for Business sits at 1,223.65 and ChrisUMD23 at 1,263.15, a gap of 39.5 that was 12.79 a week ago. ChrisUMD23's best lineup was 130.15 in a blowout loss, Open for Business's was 103.45. Open for Business's first belongs to Cheesehead10 and projects at an average slot of 2.26. ChrisUMD23's belongs to Murrdawgs and projects at 3.33. Meanwhile NotGomes owns the 2027 firsts from degr and Bijan al Gaib, and both of those teams won this week. Rough Sunday to be a draft pick on that roster.

games.h: PhilthyPhil Finishes Early, PerryCock Finishes First
t: PhilthyPhil had every single starter in the early Sunday window, which is a great way to lead a fantasy game by 68.65 points and a terrible way to keep that lead. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 46.2 in Detroit's 35-10 win over New England, C.J. Stroud added 28.55, Bhayshul Tuten chipped in 20.3, and Phil closed the laptop at 151.55. Then he sat there for three more windows like a guy who brought his whole paycheck to the casino before lunch.

PerryCock showed up after the early games. Christian McCaffrey scored 48.3 on a 22.6 projection in the 46-40 shootout between San Francisco and Dallas, which cut the deficit to 20.35. Ja'Marr Chase finished it on Sunday night with 34.1 in Cincinnati's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh. Final: 165.3 to 151.55. A 68.65-point comeback with Bryce Young scoring 10.1 on a 25.1 projection, which is like winning a footrace with one shoe.

Now the part Phil is going to hear about in the group chat. Deebo Samuel Sr. scored 25.9 and Ryan Flournoy scored 19.1, both on the bench, while Christian Watson (6.7) and Denzel Boston (2.6) started. Sleeper had the starters ahead, 26.4 projected points to 20.0, so the call was defensible. It was also wrong, again. The curse took a week off from the quarterback room and moved down the hall to the receivers. Phil's best lineup was 189.25, which wins by 23.95, and Phil left a league-high 37.7 on the pine.

PerryCock is 5-5 with three straight wins, playoff odds up from 82% to 91%, and second in the points race. Phil is still 7-3 and second in the standings, but the bye odds dipped from 69% to 64%. One man watched this game with total peace: the commissioner, who owns both teams' 2027 firsts and wanted them both to lose.
games.v: PhilthyPhil scored 151.55 before the late games kicked off and still lost. The games keep going after lunch, Phil.

games.h: Murrdawgs Sell Derrick Henry on Thursday, Score 220.85 Against Him on Sunday
t: Last Thursday, Murrdawgs Massage Parlor sent Derrick Henry to ChrisUMD23 for a 2029 first. The schedule, which has a sense of humor, made them play each other this week. Henry got his revenge game on Monday night: 19.0 points, 3.6 over his projection. He also lost by 97.9. Revenge was delivered, signed for, and returned to sender.

Murrdawgs led by 77.2 before Sunday even started, with Cam Skattebo (27.2), Isaiah Likely (29.7) and Stefon Diggs (20.3) all eating in the Thursday game between Washington and the Giants. ChrisUMD23 actually went ahead by 7.25 after the early Sunday games behind Emmett Johnson (37.1 on a 16.7 projection) and Jared Goff (31.45). It lasted one window. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 33.1, Blake Corum 22.9, and Joe Burrow dropped 45.25 on Sunday night. The 220.85 is the highest score of the 2026 season, beating Bad Bunny's Bush's 201.35 from Week 8.

Chris started David Montgomery, who had no Sleeper projection, scored 0.0, and is now listed out with a groin injury. Alvin Kamara, the man who started on a bye in Week 8, scored 16.4 on a 6.3 projection, so at least the calendar got checked this time. Murrdawgs made their own blunder: Tony Pollard, acquired from ChrisUMD23 back in Week 6, scored 23.9 on the bench while Jadarian Price started and scored 11.4, and Sleeper had Pollard projected higher, 12.2 to 9.0. Didn't matter. Nothing mattered.

Murrdawgs move into first, with bye odds up from 43% to 56%. ChrisUMD23 falls to 3-7, 11th, three straight losses. One catch for Connorj22: Murrdawgs own ChrisUMD23's 2027 first, and Chris's 130.15 best lineup nudged that pick later, to an average slot of 3.33. Beat the man, sure. Just don't make him look good doing it.
games.v: Murrdawgs sold Henry, kept Chris's first, and scored 220.85 in the revenge game. Chris got a running back and a receipt.

games.h: 142.15 Points: The Biggest Beating of the Season, Courtesy of a Former Employee
t: 142.15. That's the margin. That's the biggest blowout of the 2026 season, passing the 125.2-point loss Geno-Cide Smith took in Week 8. Bijan al Gaib scored 215.1, the second-highest total of the year, and Open for Business scored 72.95. This website is legally required to call it a game.

Trevor Lawrence (38.3) and Parker Washington (30.2) turned Jacksonville's 40-23 win in Tennessee into a 68.5-point stack. George Pickens scored 45.5 on a 13.6 projection in the San Francisco-Dallas shootout, the biggest overperformance in the league. Chase Brown added 28.3 on Sunday night. And Amon-Ra St. Brown, who came over from NotGomes in the big Week 5 trade, scored 25.8 against the team that traded him. Zach Charbonnet, who went the other way in that deal, scored 9.4.

Open for Business got 0.0 from Demarcus Robinson (projected 8.5), 1.0 from Germie Bernard (projected 11.1) and 2.4 from Tyler Warren (projected 12.7). Cyrus Allen scored 12.4 on the bench on a 1.6 projection, and nobody in America was starting that. Omarion Hampton's 19.5 on Monday night was the lone highlight. That's four straight losses, and the playoff odds went from 8% to 3%.

Here's the twist of the knife: NotGomes owns Bijan al Gaib's 2027 first. Every Bijan win makes that pick worse, and Bijan has won four straight, with bye odds up from 16% to 36%. On the bright side for somebody, Open for Business's own first belongs to Cheesehead10, and a 103.45 best lineup was exactly what Cheesehead10 wanted to see.
games.v: Bijan al Gaib hung 215.1 on the team holding its first-round pick. NotGomes watched that pick get worse in real time.

games.h: Brock Purdy Knocks First Place Off the Top Shelf
t: Bad Bunny's Bush walked into Sunday at 7-2 and in first place. degr walked in at 3-6 with 16% playoff odds. You can guess where this is going, and you'd be right: degr 103.65, Bad Bunny's Bush 93.6, and jambosti is now third.

Bad Bunny's Bush led by 17.4 after the early games. Then Brock Purdy scored 43.55 on a 28.9 projection in San Francisco's 46-40 win in Dallas, and with Ashton Jeanty adding 10.4, the late window turned that 17.4 deficit into a 30.35-point degr lead. Tee Higgins and Jaylen Warren got 20.7 back on Sunday night, which was 9.65 short.

The bench will haunt this one. Matthew Stafford scored 28.25 on the bench while Josh Allen scored 26.3, but Sleeper had Allen up 29.4 to 21.7, so that's a fine call. The real killers were Sam LaPorta (2.6 on a 12.1 projection) and Jaylen Warren (9.1 on 17.1). Bad Bunny's best lineup was 110.55, which wins. Woody Marks scored 7.5 and has since been ruled out with a concussion. And the $1 waiver add, Chimere Dike, scored 4.1 on the bench, so James Conner can rest easy.

Trade check: A.J. Brown, who went from Bad Bunny's Bush to degr in Week 6, started against his old team, scored 4.7 on a 14.4 projection, and has since been ruled out with a hamstring injury. degr also started Keaton Mitchell (0.4, projected 6.2) over Rhamondre Stevenson (1.5, projected 12.5), a real blunder that cost a whole 1.1 points. degr has won two straight and the playoff odds went from 16% to 26%. Bad Bunny's bye odds went from 68% to 38%.
games.v: degr beat first place with one quarterback and a prayer. Bad Bunny's Bush lost it with LaPorta in the lineup and the bye seat out the door.

games.h: Willy Had 100.75 Points of Quarterback and Picked the Right Half
t: Willy had 100.75 points of quarterback this week and could only use one of them. Patrick Mahomes scored 50.9 in Kansas City's 35-13 win in Atlanta, the top score by any player in the league. Dak Prescott scored 49.85 on the bench. Sleeper had Mahomes up 25.9 to 23.9, Willy went with Mahomes, and Geno-Cide Smith finally won a coin flip by 1.05 points. After losing the two closest games of the season in Weeks 6 and 7, the man has earned one.

CeeDeez Nutz has the opposite problem, again. Drake Maye scored 3.5 on a 29.2 projection, the worst dud in the league, in New England's 35-10 loss to Detroit, and he has since been ruled out with an ankle injury. Cam Ward scored 25.45 on the bench. Sleeper had Maye ahead by 14.0, so DylanDaKing gets a pass on the call. The football gods do not get a pass. This is the team that left 84.7 points of quarterback on the bench in Week 8, and it just dropped Kyler Murray for Ty Johnson, who scored 1.4 on the bench.

Chuba Hubbard went for 34.2 and CeeDeez Nutz led by 1.1 when the late games ended. The problem: CeeDeez's lineup was finished and Geno-Cide Smith still had two guys left. DK Metcalf scored 15.4 on Sunday night, Zay Flowers added 11.4 on Monday, and the final was 141.7 to 116.0. Mark Andrews scoring 16.2 on the bench behind Tucker Kraft (2.9) didn't help either, though Sleeper liked Kraft by 3.8.

Geno-Cide Smith is 5-5, two straight wins, sixth place, and holding the last playoff spot with 21% odds, up from 16%. CeeDeez Nutz drops from fifth to seventh and its playoff odds fall from 59% to 35%, a 24-point cliff.
games.v: Geno-Cide Smith finally won a quarterback coin flip. CeeDeez Nutz keeps losing them without even flipping.

games.h: The Commissioner Starts Adam Randall Again
t: For the second straight week, the commissioner of this league started Adam Randall. Adam Randall is on injured reserve. Sleeper projected him for 0. He scored 0.0. Efton Chism III joined him with 0.0 on a 2.8 projection, so Matty Ice is back to playing with two empty chairs. The kicker: Matt's best lineup was 70.55, only 3.0 better, because Jack Bech was the only thing on the bench worth plugging in. The lineup was about as good as this roster allows, and that's the scary part.

Cheesehead10 led 41.85 to 7.4 after Thursday night, thanks mostly to Jayden Daniels (29.25), and Matty Ice never got closer than 20.2. Brock Bowers scored 3.8 on a 15.2 projection and has since been ruled out with an ankle injury. Malik Nabers had 7.4 and Tetairoa McMillan, the Week 8 trade prize, had 6.5 on a 15.7 projection. Jordyn Tyson (19.0 on a 9.1 projection) and Samaje Perine (13.9 on 6.1) were the only two guys who read the script. Tre' Harris tacked on 13.6 for Cheesehead10 on Monday night. Final: 101.35 to 67.55.

Then Cheesehead10 did something very Cheesehead10. Ollie Gordon II scored 15.5 in this game, and that same Sunday afternoon he was traded to PhilthyPhil for a 2027 third and a 2028 second. Cheesehead10 is 5-5 with 26% playoff odds, the most valuable roster in the league, seven firsts, and apparently no interest in pretending to be a contender.

Matty Ice is 1-9 with five straight losses and the lowest score of the week. The 1.01 is locked in every simulation with an 846.75 Max PF. That pick is the safest thing in this league. The running back slot is the least safe.
games.v: Matty Ice started an injured reserve running back for the second week in a row. The 1.01 is safe. The lineup is a crime scene.

rules.source: League of Ordinary Gentlemen rules document
rules.onlyRule: Be engaged. In the offseason, check the app occasionally and respond in a timely manner when people have trade inquiries.
rules.ruleChanges: Anyone can propose a rule change. Bring it up in the group chat or in Sleeper, and the league votes on it if it has merit with the group.

draft.format: Slow rookie draft, usually within one to two weeks of the NFL draft. Each manager has a 24-hour window to make a pick.
draft.nonPlayoff: Non-playoff teams pick 1.01 through 1.06 in reverse order of Maximum Points For.
draft.playoff: Playoff teams are placed by the consolation and title games: 5th-place game winner 1.07, loser 1.08; 3rd-place game winner 1.09, loser 1.10; runner-up 1.11; champion 1.12.
draft.pfException: If the regular-season scoring champion does not reach the championship game, that team automatically picks 1.10, because it walked away from the season with money. The remaining playoff teams move up accordingly.
